# PTXprint User Interface Manual (AI support edition)

Generated 2026-10-17 from the PTXprint source code and the explanations in docs/uimanual/content.

> **Notes for the AI support assistant**
>
> * This manual describes every setting in the PTXprint user interface (UI). Each setting lists
>   *where* it is (tab › section), *which view level* shows it, its *tooltip*, and a plain-language
>   explanation.
> * Most PTXprint users are **not technical**, and many speak English as a second or third language.
>   Answer in short, simple sentences. Give click-by-click directions using the tab and section
>   names exactly as written here.
> * **Do not tell users to edit configuration files (ptxprint.cfg), .sty or .tex files, or run
>   commands.** Every answer should be achievable in the PTXprint window. If something truly
>   cannot be done in the UI, say so and suggest contacting ptxprint_support@sil.org.
> * If a user cannot find a setting, check its *View level*. Many settings are hidden in the
>   Mini and Basic views. Tell the user how to change the view level (see "View levels").
> * Some settings are greyed out or hidden until another setting is turned on. This is shown as
>   "Only available when ..." and "Hidden until ...".
> * "Internal ID" and "Config key" lines are for support staff. They help you match a setting
>   that appears in a user's settings file or log to the place in the UI. Do not ask users about them.

# About this manual

## What PTXprint is

PTXprint is a program that makes print-ready PDF files of Scripture. It takes the text from a
Paratext project and lays it out on pages: with columns, headings, chapter and verse numbers,
footnotes, cross-references, pictures, headers and footers. You can use the PDF for checking and
proofreading, or send it to a printer to make a book.

Behind the scenes, PTXprint uses a typesetting program called **XeTeX**. XeTeX does the work of
placing every letter and line on the page. You never need to use XeTeX yourself. You make all
your choices in the PTXprint window, and PTXprint tells XeTeX what to do.

PTXprint never changes your Paratext text. It reads the text, makes a temporary copy, and
typesets that copy. To correct the words of the text, use Paratext.

## Who this manual is for

This manual is for everyone who uses the PTXprint window: translators, typesetters, project
leaders and support staff. You do not need to know anything about typesetting or computers to use
it.

* Every instruction in this manual can be done in the PTXprint window. You never need to edit
  files by hand or type commands.
* Some sections are marked **advanced**. They explain how to type special codes in the few places
  where PTXprint gives you a text box for them (for example the front matter). You can skip these
  sections until you need them.
* Technical words are explained the first time they appear in a chapter. They are also listed in
  the **Glossary of terms** at the end of the manual.

## How this manual is organised

The manual starts with two general chapters. Then there is one chapter for each tab of the
PTXprint window, in the same order as the tabs. After that come chapters about the PDF Preview
window, importing settings and getting help. The manual ends with step-by-step tasks, solutions
to problems, and a glossary.

1. **About this manual** – this chapter.
2. **Getting started with PTXprint** – a first walk-through: from opening PTXprint to your first PDF.
3. **The main window, menu and view levels** – the parts of the window, configurations, view
   levels, and how PTXprint saves your settings.
4. **Basic tab** – choose the project, the configuration and the books to print.
5. **Layout tab** – page size, margins, columns, font size and line spacing.
6. **Fonts+Script tab** – fonts, writing system, hyphenation and spacing.
7. **Body tab** – what is printed from each book (introductions, headings, verse numbers…).
8. **Notes+Refs tab** – footnotes, cross-references and study notes.
9. **Header+Footer tab** – the running header and footer, and page numbers.
10. **Pictures tab** – illustrations and maps.
11. **Diglot tab (two or more languages)** – two or more texts side by side.
12. **Tabs+Borders tab** – thumb tabs and decorative borders.
13. **Styles tab** – the look of each kind of text (each USFM marker).
14. **Advanced tab** – settings for experienced users.
15. **View+Edit tab** – front matter, the adjustment list, and the files PTXprint makes.
16. **Peripherals tab (front and back matter)** – front matter, table of contents, colophon, maps and covers.
17. **Publications tab** – a list of publications that you can print together.
18. **Finishing tab** – PDF type for the printer, crop marks, booklets and comparing PDFs.
19. **Printers tab** – price estimates and orders from print companies.
20. **PDF Preview window, layout analysis and page filling** – look at the PDF and fix the layout of pages.
21. **Importing settings** – copy settings from a PDF, an archive or another configuration.
22. **Help tab and getting support** – find your files, and ask for help.
23. **How do I...? (step-by-step tasks)** – short instructions for common jobs.
24. **Problems and solutions** – what to do when something goes wrong.
25. **Glossary of terms** – the meaning of the words used in this manual.

Most tab chapters have the same parts:

* **What this tab is for** – when you would use the tab.
* One section for each area of the tab, using the names you see on the screen.
* **Common tasks** – numbered steps for the things people do most often.
* **Common problems** – what you see, why it happens, and what to change.
* **Settings reference** – a list of every setting on the tab (see below).

## How to read a settings-reference entry

At the end of each tab chapter, the **Settings reference** lists every setting (check box, list,
number box, button and so on) in that part of PTXprint. Each entry starts with the name of the
setting as you see it on the screen. Then it gives some or all of these facts:

* **Where** – the path to the setting: the tab, then the area or sub-tab. For example:
  *Layout tab › Page Setup*.
* **Type** – what kind of control it is, for example a check box, a drop-down list, a number box or
  a button. For a check box, it also says if it is ticked or not ticked by default.
* **Description** – a short name for the setting, when the label on the screen does not say
  enough.
* **Next to the label** – the label that is beside the control on the screen, when this is
  different from the name of the entry.
* **View level** – in which view levels you can see the setting (see below).
* **Values** – for a number box: the lowest and highest number you can type, and the default value.
* **Choices** – for a drop-down list: the items in the list.
* **Only available when** – the setting is greyed out until another setting is turned on.
* **Greyed out when** – the setting cannot be used while another setting is turned on.
* **Hidden until** – the setting is not shown until another setting is ticked.
* **Tooltip** – the help text that PTXprint shows when you hold the mouse over the setting.
* **Explanation** – a description in plain words: what the setting does, when to use it, a
  sensible value, and what to watch out for.

If you cannot find a setting in the window, look first at its **View level**, then at **Only
available when** and **Hidden until**.

## A short note about view levels

PTXprint has hundreds of settings, but most people need only a few of them. So PTXprint can hide
the settings that you do not need. This is called the **view level**. There are four view levels:
**Mini**, **Basic**, **Default** and **Full**. **Mini** shows the fewest settings. **Full** shows
every setting.

To change the view level, click the **☰** button at the top-right of the window, point to
**View Level**, and choose a level.

A hidden setting still works. It keeps its value and it still changes the PDF. So if the PDF
does not look the way you expect, change to the **Full** view and check the settings again.

In this manual, a note such as "(Default and Full views)" tells you which view levels show a
setting. For more about view levels, see the chapter **The main window, menu and view levels**.


# Getting started with PTXprint

## About this chapter

This chapter is for people who are using PTXprint for the first time. It takes you step by step
from opening PTXprint to your first PDF. Then it shows you how to change a few common things, and
how to keep different sets of settings for different kinds of output.

You do not need to read the rest of the manual before you start. Each step tells you which chapter
to read if you want to know more.

In this chapter, "pt" means point. One point is about 0.35 mm. Font sizes and line spacing are
given in points.

## Before you start

Check these things before you open PTXprint:

1. **You have a Paratext project.** PTXprint prints the text of a Paratext project. The project
   must be on this computer. If you use Send/Receive in Paratext, do a Send/Receive first, so that
   you have the latest text.
2. **The text has no serious marker errors.** PTXprint uses the USFM markers in the text (for
   example `\p` for a paragraph or `\v` for a verse). Run the Basic Checks in Paratext. Marker
   errors can stop PTXprint or give strange results.
3. **The fonts are installed.** Install the fonts that your project needs on this computer. Install
   them **for all users**. If a font is installed only for one user, PTXprint may not find it.
4. **You do not have a project, but want to practise?** You can still use PTXprint. It can install
   a sample English Bible (the Berean Standard Bible) for you. See "Get a text to practise with"
   in the **Basic tab** chapter.

## Open PTXprint

1. Start PTXprint in the same way as other programs on your computer, for example from the
   Windows Start menu.
2. The main PTXprint window opens. It has:
   * **tabs** across the top (**Basic**, **Layout**, **Fonts+Script** and others). Each tab holds
     one group of settings;
   * the **☰** button at the top-right, for the main menu;
   * a **bar at the bottom** with the **Save**, **Print (Make PDF)** and **Quit** buttons.

The first time PTXprint starts, it uses the **Default** view level. This view shows most tabs and
settings. If the window looks too full, you can change to a simpler view: click **☰**, point to
**View Level**, and click **Basic View** or **Mini View**. Hidden settings still work. See the
chapter **The main window, menu and view levels**.

If PTXprint does not show your projects in the **Project** list, it may be looking in the wrong
folder. See "Use projects from another Paratext folder" in the chapter **Help tab and getting
support**.

## Choose the project and the configuration

Everything starts on the **Basic** tab.

1. Click the **Basic** tab.
2. In the **Project** list, choose your Paratext project. PTXprint shows the full name of the
   project next to the list.
3. In the **Layout Configuration** area, look at the **Name** list. The first time, it shows
   **Default**.

A **configuration** is a named set of PTXprint settings for one project: page size, fonts,
pictures and so on. Every project has a configuration called **Default**. You can make more
configurations later (see "Keep different settings for different outputs" below). For now, use
**Default**.

## Choose the books

On the **Basic** tab, in the **What to Print** area:

1. Click **Single Book**.
2. Choose a book from the list. For your first PDF, choose a short book, for example Ruth, Jonah,
   Philippians or Jude. A short book prints quickly.
3. To print only some chapters, type the first chapter in **From Chapter** and the last chapter in
   **To**.

Later, to print several books, click **Select Multiple Books...**, click the books you want, and
click **OK**. See the **Basic tab** chapter for more ways to choose books and passages.

## Make your first PDF

1. Click **Print (Make PDF)** at the bottom right of the window (or press **Ctrl+P**).
2. PTXprint first saves your settings. Then it makes the PDF. A progress bar shows that it is
   working. This can take from a few seconds to a few minutes, depending on the number of books
   and pictures.
3. When PTXprint has finished, the **PDF Preview** window opens and shows the PDF.

If a message appears instead of the PDF, read it carefully. Two common messages at the start are:

* **"No books to print"** – no book is selected. Choose a book on the **Basic** tab.
* **"One or more fonts have not been set yet"** – go to the **Fonts+Script** tab and choose a font
  for the main text (see "Change the main font" below).

## Look at the PDF in the preview

The **PDF Preview** window shows the pages of your PDF.

* Use the arrow buttons at the top, the **Left/Right arrow** keys, or the mouse wheel to move from
  page to page.
* Use the **Zoom** box, or hold **Ctrl** and turn the mouse wheel, to make the page bigger or
  smaller.
* Tick **Book View** (or press **Ctrl+B**) to see two facing pages side by side, as in a printed
  book.
* The title bar shows the name of the PDF file and the time when it was made. Check it, so you
  know that you are looking at the newest PDF.
* Click **Show main PTXprint settings** (or press **Alt+S**) to go back to the main window.

If you close the Preview window, it is only hidden. It comes back the next time you print. The
Preview window can do much more, for example find layout problems and fix them. See the chapter
**PDF Preview window, layout analysis and page filling**.

## Change a few common things

After each change, click **Print (Make PDF)** again to see the result.

### Change the page size

1. Click the **Layout** tab.
2. In the **Page Setup** area, open the **Page Size** list.
3. Choose a size, for example **148mm, 210mm (A5)**. Or type your own size: the width, a comma,
   then the height, for example `140mm, 216mm`.

Ask your printer for the exact page size (the "trim size") before you do a lot of work. If you
change the page size later, every line of the book moves.

### Change the main font

1. Click the **Fonts+Script** tab.
2. In the **Font Configuration** area, click the **Select Font...** button next to **Regular**.
3. The **Pick a Font (and Typeface)** dialog opens. Type part of the font name in the search box,
   then click the font in the list.
4. Click **OK**.

PTXprint then fills in the **Bold**, **Italic** and **Bold Italic** fonts for you from the same
font family. If some characters print as empty boxes, the font does not have those characters.
See the **Fonts+Script tab** chapter.

### Change the font size

1. Click the **Layout** tab.
2. In the **Page Setup** area, change **Base Font Size (pt)**. For example, 11 pt is a common size
   for the main text.

When **Lock Ratio** is ticked (the normal setting), PTXprint changes the **Base Line Spacing (pt)**
with the font size, so that the page keeps the same look. Headings, footnotes and verse numbers
also grow or shrink with the main text. See the **Layout tab** chapter.

### Change between one and two columns

1. Click the **Layout** tab.
2. Tick **Two Column Layout** for two columns, or untick it for one column.

PTXprint changes the **Base Indent** for you when you change the number of columns.

### Turn pictures on or off

The **Pictures** tab is not shown in the **Mini** view. If you cannot see it, click **☰** ›
**View Level** › **Basic View** (or a higher view).

1. Click the **Pictures** tab.
2. On the **Global Options** sub-tab, tick **Include Pictures (illustrations)** to print the
   pictures, or untick it to leave them out.

The first time you turn pictures on, PTXprint needs a list of the pictures (the PicList). It makes
this list from the `\fig` entries in your Paratext text. See "Show the pictures that are in the
Paratext text" in the **Pictures tab** chapter. While you are working on a draft, choose **Low
Resolution (Smaller File)** on the same sub-tab, so that the PDF stays small.

## Keep different settings for different outputs

You often need more than one kind of PDF from the same project. For example:

* a **draft** for checking, with wide spacing, "DRAFT" on each page and small pictures;
* a **final** PDF for the printer, with high-quality pictures and the PDF type that the printer
  asks for.

Do not change one configuration back and forth. Make a separate configuration for each kind of
output. Each configuration remembers its own settings.

### Make a new configuration

1. Click **Save** at the bottom of the window, so that your latest changes are kept.
2. On the **Basic** tab, in the **Layout Configuration** area, click the **Save As** button (the
   icon next to the **Name** list).
3. The **Save Current Configuration As...** dialog opens. Type a name, for example `Draft` or
   `Final_A5`. Use only letters, numbers, brackets `( )`, underscores `_` and hyphens `-`. Do not
   use spaces.
4. Click **OK**. PTXprint makes the new configuration as a copy of the current settings, and
   changes to it.
5. Now change the settings for this kind of output. The other configuration stays as it was.

### Change to another configuration

1. Click **Save** first. PTXprint does **not** save the current configuration when you choose
   another one.
2. On the **Basic** tab, choose the configuration in the **Name** list.

When a configuration is finished, you can lock it with a password so that nobody changes it by
mistake. See "Protect a finished configuration" in the **Basic tab** chapter.

## How PTXprint saves your settings

* **Save** (or **Ctrl+S**) saves the settings of the current configuration.
* **Print (Make PDF)** always saves the settings first, then makes the PDF.
* When you choose a different **project**, PTXprint saves the current configuration first.
* When you choose a different **configuration**, PTXprint does **not** save first. Click **Save**
  before you change.
* **Quit** closes PTXprint **without saving**. Click **Save** before you click **Quit**.

PTXprint keeps the configurations inside the Paratext project. So when you use Send/Receive in
Paratext, the other people on your team get the same configurations.

## Where the PDF is saved

PTXprint saves the PDF inside the Paratext project, in a folder called `local\ptxprint`. This
folder is not shared by Send/Receive. The file name is made from the project code, the
configuration name and the books, for example `ABC_Default_JHN_ptxp.pdf`.

You do not need to remember the folder. To open it, use one of these ways:

* Click the **Open folder containing the PDF** button in the bar at the bottom of the main window
  (**Default** and **Full** views).
* On the **Help** tab, click the blue link next to **Output PDF Location**.
* In the PDF Preview window, click **Open folder containing the PDF**.

PTXprint makes the PDF again each time you print, with the same name. If you want to keep a PDF
(for example the one you sent to a consultant), copy it to another folder, or click **Save the PDF
with a different name** in the PDF Preview window.

## When something goes wrong

* **Read the message.** PTXprint shows a message in a window, or in the status line above the
  bottom bar. The message often tells you what to change.
* **Check the view level.** If a tab or setting has disappeared, the view level may be too low.
  Click **☰** › **View Level** › **Full View**. You can also type the name of a setting in the
  **Search for settings** box at the bottom-left of the window.
* **Check the "Common problems" section** of the chapter about the tab you were using.
* **Look in the chapter "Problems and solutions"** for problems that are not about one tab.
* **Ask for help.** The chapter **Help tab and getting support** explains how to ask the Support
  Agent, the PTXprint User Community, or the support team, and how to make an archive file that
  the support team can use to see your problem.

## What to read next

* **The main window, menu and view levels** – more about configurations, view levels and saving.
* **Basic tab** and **Layout tab** – the most important settings for every publication.
* **How do I...? (step-by-step tasks)** – short instructions for many common jobs.


# The main window, menu and view levels

## What this part of PTXprint is for

The main window is where you do all your work in PTXprint. It has three parts:

* **The tabs** across the top (**Basic**, **Layout**, **Fonts+Script**, **Body** and so on). Each tab holds one group of settings.
* **The ☰ main menu** button at the top-right corner, next to the tabs. It holds settings about PTXprint itself, not about your book: how to show the PDF, the **View Level**, the interface **Language**, and links to **Donate** and **Give Feedback**.
* **The bar at the bottom of the window**. It holds the **Search for settings** box, the button to open the output folder, the **Quick Run** and **Layout Only** check boxes, and the **Save**, **Print (Make PDF)** and **Quit** buttons.

This chapter also explains three ideas that you need everywhere in PTXprint: **configurations**, **view levels**, and how PTXprint **saves** your settings.

## Projects and configurations

A **project** is a Paratext project – the Scripture text that you want to print. You choose the project on the **Basic** tab, in the **Project** list.

A **configuration** (also called a "layout" or "config") is a named set of PTXprint settings for one project. One project can have many configurations. For example, you can have one configuration called `Default` for a draft, one called `NT_A5` for a small New Testament, and one called `Large_Print`. Each configuration remembers its own page size, fonts, pictures, styles, front matter and so on.

* Every project has a configuration called **Default**. You cannot delete or lock it, but you can reset it.
* You choose, create, lock, copy and delete configurations on the **Basic** tab, in the **Layout Configuration** area. See the chapter about the Basic tab.
* PTXprint keeps the configurations inside the Paratext project folder. So when you use **Send/Receive** in Paratext, other people on the team get the same configurations.

## How PTXprint saves your settings

* Click **Save** (or press **Ctrl+S**) to save the settings of the current configuration.
* Click **Print (Make PDF)** (or press **Ctrl+P**). PTXprint **always saves** the settings first, and then makes the PDF.
* When you choose a **different project** in the **Project** list, PTXprint saves the current configuration first.
* When you choose a **different configuration** in the **Layout Configuration** list, PTXprint does **not** save the current one first. Click **Save** before you change to another configuration, or your recent changes are lost.
* **Quit** closes PTXprint **without saving**. If you want to keep your changes, click **Save** or **Print (Make PDF)** before you click **Quit**.
* If a configuration is **locked** with a password, PTXprint does not save changes to it. You can still change settings on the screen and make a PDF, but the changes are not kept.

Some things are remembered for you (the user) and not for the configuration: the view level, the interface language, the **Show PDF** choice and the **Quick Run** setting. These stay the same for all projects and configurations.

## View levels

PTXprint has hundreds of settings. Most people need only a few of them. So PTXprint can hide the settings that you do not need. This is the **view level**. There are four view levels:

| View level | What you see | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| **Mini** | Only the **Basic**, **Layout**, **Fonts+Script** and **Help** tabs, and only the most important settings on them: project, books, configuration name, page size, font size, two columns, the main font. | A first look at PTXprint, or a quick draft. |
| **Basic** | Adds the **Body**, **Notes+Refs**, **Header+Footer** and **Pictures** tabs, and more settings on each tab (margins, line spacing, bold and italic fonts, the **Import Settings** button…). | Most simple publications. |
| **Default** | Adds the **Diglot**, **Tabs+Borders**, **Styles**, **Advanced**, **View+Edit**, **Peripherals**, **Publications** and **Finishing** tabs, and many more settings on all tabs. | Most typesetters. This is the view level that PTXprint uses the first time it starts. |
| **Full** | Shows every setting, including the **Printers** tab. | Experienced users who need special settings. |

**How to change the view level:** click the **☰** button (top-right), point to **View Level**, and click **Mini View**, **Basic View**, **Default View** or **Full View**. The current level is shown in blue and bold in that list. The change happens at once. You do not need to restart PTXprint.

**Hidden settings still work.** When you change to a lower view level, PTXprint only *hides* the settings. It does not change them. A hidden setting keeps its value, it is still saved with the configuration, and it still changes the PDF. For example, if you turned on pictures or a diglot in the **Default** view and then change to the **Mini** view, the pictures or the diglot will still be in the PDF, even though you cannot see the tab. If the PDF looks different from what you expect, change to the **Full** view and check the settings again.

**Search finds hidden settings.** If you use the **Search for settings** box and choose a setting that is hidden at your view level, PTXprint changes to a higher view level so that it can show you the setting.

## Tab labels and highlighted settings

PTXprint uses colour and bold text to help you see what is turned on or changed:

* The tab that is open now has a light blue background and a bold label.
* Some tab labels turn **blue** when their main feature is turned on. For example: **Pictures** is blue when pictures are included, **Diglot** is blue when the diglot is turned on, **Peripherals** is blue when front matter, back matter PDFs or a table of contents is turned on, **Finishing** is blue when you print more than one page per sheet, and **Advanced** is blue when one of its special files or options (custom script, changes file, extra TeX or style files, interlinear) is turned on. On **Fonts+Script**, the word "Fonts" is blue when coloured text is enabled. On **Notes+Refs**, "Refs" is blue when an extended cross-reference list is used. On **Tabs+Borders**, "Tabs" or "Borders" is blue when thumb tabs or decorative borders are turned on.
* Some number settings (mostly on the **Layout** tab: font size, line spacing, margins, column gutter, header and footer positions and similar) have a label that becomes **bold** when the value is different from the PTXprint default. This helps you see quickly which values you have changed.

## The bottom bar

From left to right, the bar at the bottom of the window has:

* **Search for settings** – type a word to find a setting.
* **Open folder containing the PDF** – opens the output folder. (Default and Full views.)
* **Quick Run** and **Layout Only** – two check boxes that make printing faster.
* **Print** – only appears when you are looking at the secondary text of a diglot.
* **Save**, **Print (Make PDF)** and **Quit**.

Above the bar, a **status line** sometimes appears with a message from PTXprint (for example "No books to print"). Click **Dismiss** to hide it.

When a newer version of PTXprint is available, a **Check for updates...** button can appear at the top-right, next to the ☰ button. (PTXprint checks at most once a day, only on Windows, and only if Internet use is allowed on the **Advanced** tab.)

## The ☰ main menu

* **Show PDF** – choose what happens with the PDF after printing:
  * **Preview Pane** – PTXprint shows the PDF in its own preview window. This is the usual choice. PTXprint can also use the preview for some editing tools.
  * **System Viewer** – the PDF opens in the PDF program on your computer.
  * **Output Folder** – PTXprint opens the folder that holds the PDF.
* **View Level** – see "View levels" above.
* **Language** – the language of the PTXprint menus and labels.
* **Donate** and **Give Feedback** – open a web page.

## Common tasks

### See more (or fewer) settings

1. Click the **☰** button at the top-right of the window.
2. Point to **View Level**.
3. Click **Full View** to see every setting, or **Mini View** to see only the most important ones.

### Find a setting when you do not know which tab it is on

1. Click in the **Search for settings** box at the bottom-left (or press **Ctrl+F**).
2. Type a word, for example `margin` or `footnote`, and press **Enter**.
3. A short list of settings appears above the box. Click the one you want.
4. PTXprint opens the right tab and highlights the setting. If the setting was hidden, PTXprint changes the view level so you can see it.
5. To clear the search, click the small clear icon at the right end of the box.

### Make a PDF

1. On the **Basic** tab, choose the project, the configuration and the books.
2. Click **Print (Make PDF)** (or press **Ctrl+P**).
3. Wait. A progress bar shows that PTXprint is working. When it is finished, the PDF appears (in the preview pane, the system viewer or the output folder, depending on **Show PDF**).

### Make the PDF faster while you work on the layout

1. Tick **Quick Run** (or press **Ctrl+Q**). PTXprint runs the typesetting only once.
2. If you only change layout settings (spacing, margins, styles), you can also tick **Layout Only** (Default and Full views).
3. When the layout is ready, untick **Quick Run** and click **Print (Make PDF)** one more time. This makes sure the table of contents, page references and other details are correct.

### Show the PDF in another program

1. Click **☰** › **Show PDF**.
2. Click **System Viewer**.

### Find the PDF file on your computer

1. Click the **Open folder containing the PDF** button at the bottom of the window (Default and Full views), or choose **☰** › **Show PDF** › **Output Folder**.
2. The folder opens. The PDF files for this project are in it.

### Change the language of PTXprint

1. Click **Save** first, so you do not lose changes.
2. Click **☰** › **Language** and click a language.
3. PTXprint closes its window and opens it again in the new language, with the same project and configuration.

## Common problems

### A tab or setting that I used before has disappeared

**Likely cause:** The view level is lower than before. **What to do:** Click **☰** › **View Level** › **Default View** or **Full View**. Or type the name of the setting in **Search for settings**.

### The PDF has pictures (or a diglot, borders, thumb tabs…) but I cannot find the setting

**Likely cause:** The setting was turned on in a higher view level, and now that tab is hidden. Hidden settings still work. **What to do:** Change to **Full View** and turn the feature off on its tab.

### I lost my changes after I chose another configuration

**Likely cause:** PTXprint does not save the current configuration when you choose another one in the **Layout Configuration** list. **What to do:** Always click **Save** (or **Print (Make PDF)**) before you change to another configuration.

### I lost my changes after I clicked Quit

**Likely cause:** **Quit** does not save. **What to do:** Click **Save** before **Quit**.

### The Print (Make PDF) and Save buttons are greyed out

**Likely cause:** PTXprint cannot print yet. For example, no project is selected, or another problem is shown in the status line. **What to do:** Read the message in the status line above the bottom bar. Choose a project on the **Basic** tab and fix the problem that is described.

### PTXprint says "Cannot update PDF file while it is locked!"

**Likely cause:** The old PDF is still open in another PDF program, so PTXprint cannot replace it. **What to do:** Close the PDF in the other program and click to try again. To avoid this, use **☰** › **Show PDF** › **Preview Pane**.

### PTXprint says "No books to print"

**Likely cause:** No book is selected, or the book list is empty. **What to do:** On the **Basic** tab, in **What to Print**, choose a book or click **Select Multiple Books...**.

### PTXprint says "One or more fonts have not been set yet"

**What to do:** Go to the **Fonts+Script** tab and choose a font for the main text.

### The table of contents or page numbers in the PDF are wrong

**Likely cause:** **Quick Run** is ticked, so PTXprint ran the typesetting only once. **What to do:** Untick **Quick Run** and print again.

### My change to the text in Paratext does not appear in the PDF

**Likely cause:** In most cases, PTXprint notices that the text changed and processes it again, even when **Layout Only** is ticked. If it does not, **Layout Only** may be stopping it. **What to do:** Untick **Layout Only** and print again.

### The changes I make are not kept

**Likely cause:** The configuration is locked with a password. A locked configuration is not saved. **What to do:** On the **Basic** tab, click the lock button and enter the password to unlock it. Or use **Save As** to make a new configuration.

## Settings reference: The main window, menu and view levels

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

### Main menu (top-right ☰ button)

#### Show PDF

- **Where:** Main menu (top-right ☰ button)
- **Type:** Menu button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Choose how the PDF is shown after printing: in the preview pane, in your system's PDF viewer, or by opening the output folder.

**Explanation:**

Opens a small list with three choices: **Preview Pane**, **System Viewer** and **Output Folder**. The choice in blue is the current one. When you click a choice, PTXprint uses it at once to show the last PDF, and it remembers the choice for all projects. **Preview Pane** is the best choice for most people, because PTXprint can then update the preview itself and the PDF file is not kept open by another program.

*(Internal ID: `btn_menu_showPDF`)*

#### View Level

- **Where:** Main menu (top-right ☰ button)
- **Type:** Menu button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Choose how many settings PTXprint shows. Hidden settings keep their values and still take effect.

**Explanation:**

Opens the list of view levels: **Mini View**, **Basic View**, **Default View** and **Full View**. The current level is shown in blue. The view level only changes which settings you can *see*. Hidden settings keep their values and still change the PDF. PTXprint remembers the view level for you (not for each configuration). The first time PTXprint starts, it uses the **Default View**.

*(Internal ID: `btn_menu_level`)*

#### Language

- **Where:** Main menu (top-right ☰ button)
- **Type:** Menu button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Change the language of the PTXprint user interface.

**Explanation:**

Opens the list of languages for the PTXprint interface. The current language is shown in blue. When you choose another language, PTXprint closes and opens its window again in that language, with the same project and configuration. Click **Save** first, because unsaved changes are not kept. This only changes the PTXprint menus and labels, not the language of your book.

*(Internal ID: `btn_menu_lang`)*

#### Donate

- **Where:** Main menu (top-right ☰ button)
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Donate toward PTXprint Development
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> PTXprint is a tool that is freely available to all without any restrictions. Our aim is to help people get the Scriptures out to people in formats that work best for their local context.
>
> Click to contribute toward the ongoing development and maintenance of tools by SIL Global's Language Technology Developers so that others can also benefit.
>
> https://give.sil.org/campaign/725128/donate

**Explanation:**

Opens the SIL donation web page in your web browser. If **Disable ALL Internet Use** is ticked on the **Advanced** tab, PTXprint shows a message instead of opening the page.

*(Internal ID: `btn_menu_donate`)*

#### Give Feedback

- **Where:** Main menu (top-right ☰ button)
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Link to PTXprint Feedback Form (Google Form)
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Psst! Can we have 5 minutes of your time? You could help us make PTXprint better!
>
> The developers of PTXprint would love to know how this tool is being used. What is your favorite feature? Are there any annoyances? Tell us what you like, or don't like. Tell us what you dream for in the future.
>
> Click this button to fill in the Google form or type this in a browser: https://tiny.cc/ptxprintfeedback

**Explanation:**

Opens a short online form where you can tell the PTXprint developers what you like, what is difficult, and what you would like in the future. It needs Internet access (see **Disable ALL Internet Use** on the **Advanced** tab).

Click the clear icon at the right end of the box to remove the highlight. Short, simple words (for example `margin`, `caption`, `verse`) work best. - **Where:** Main window

*(Internal ID: `btn_openFolder`)*

#### Quick Run

- **Where:** Main window
- **Type:** Checkbox (ticked by default)
- **Description:** Quick run (to speed up process)
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Enabling this option will give quicker output, but it may be less refined.
>
> PTXprint needs to rerun the typesetting process in order to ensure the Table of Contents & other dynamically updated details are accurate.
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-Q

**Explanation:**

When ticked, PTXprint runs the typesetting only once. Without it, PTXprint runs the typesetting several times (up to 5) so that the table of contents, cross-page details and page layout are correct. Tick it while you are trying out settings. Untick it for the final PDF. PTXprint remembers this setting for you, not for the configuration.

*(Internal ID: `c_quickRun`)*

#### Layout Only

- **Where:** Main window
- **Type:** Checkbox (ticked by default)
- **Description:** Layout Only (skip USFM processing)
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Re-runs page layout without regenerating or processing USFM scripture content.
>
> Useful for quick layout tweaks (+1 / −1 spacing or style changes).
>
> PTXprint still re-processes the USFM when the text has changed in Paratext, or when you change a setting that affects the text (the box then shows a dash until the next successful print).
>
> This setting is not saved with the configuration.

**Explanation:**

When ticked, PTXprint skips the step that prepares the USFM text, and only does the page layout again. This is faster when you only change layout, spacing or style settings. PTXprint still prepares the text again when it is needed, for example when the text in Paratext has changed, or when you change a setting that changes the text (such as which books, footnotes, or verse numbers to include). In that case, the box shows a dash until the next successful print. This setting is not saved with the configuration. If you tick it while the colophon is turned on, PTXprint turns the colophon off. Only shown in the **Default** and **Full** views.

*(Internal ID: `c_noupdate`)*

#### Print

- **Where:** Main window
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> The configuration displayed now is for the secondary project of the Diglot. You can use this button to create a PDF with just the secondary text to check the settings specified.
>
> Use the larger 'Return to Primary' button to get back to the primary project in order to print a diglot with both texts.

**Explanation:**

This **Print** button only appears when the main window is showing the secondary project of a diglot (after you switch to it on the **Diglot** tab). It makes a PDF of only the secondary text, so you can check its settings. At this time the large print button is called **Return to Primary**; click that to go back to the primary project and print the full diglot.

*(Internal ID: `b_print2ndDiglotText`)*

#### Save

- **Where:** Main window
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Save configuration
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Save current settings in named Configuration (set on the Basic tab).
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-S

**Explanation:**

Saves all settings of the current configuration, including the hidden ones. You do not need to click it before **Print (Make PDF)**, because printing saves too. It is greyed out when PTXprint cannot print (for example when no project is selected) and when the configuration is locked. If you have typed a new name in the configuration name box on the **Basic** tab, **Save** creates a new configuration with that name.

*(Internal ID: `btn_saveConfig`)*

#### Print (Make PDF)

- **Where:** Main window
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Create the PDF as specified (automatically saves settings).
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-P

**Explanation:**

Saves the settings and then makes the PDF. It checks first that there are books to print and that the main font is set. If an old PDF with the same name is open in another program, PTXprint asks you to close it. While PTXprint is printing, you cannot start another print. When you are looking at the secondary text of a diglot, this button is called **Return to Primary**.

*(Internal ID: `b_print`)*

#### Quit

- **Where:** Main window
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Close PTXprint without saving.
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-W

**Explanation:**

Closes PTXprint **without saving** the settings. Click **Save** first if you want to keep your changes.

*(Internal ID: `b_close`)*


# Basic tab

## What this tab is for

The **Basic** tab is the first tab in PTXprint. You come here to:

* choose the **project** (the Paratext project with the Scripture text),
* choose, save, lock, copy or delete a **configuration** (a named set of settings),
* choose **what to print** – one book, part of a book, several books, or a Bible module,
* check the **copyright and license** statement for the publication.

Start here every time. Most other settings depend on the project and configuration that you choose on this tab.

## Project

Choose your Paratext project in the **Project** list. PTXprint shows the full name of the project next to the list.

* When you change to another project, PTXprint first saves the current configuration. Then it opens the configuration that you last used with the new project (or **Default**).
* At the end of the **Project** list there is a blue item, **Import...**. It opens the **Import Scripture...** dialog. Use it when you do not have the text as a Paratext project, but you have a Scripture text bundle (a .zip file), or when you want to install the sample text (the Berean Standard Bible).

### Copyright & Licensing

(This area is only shown in the **Default** and **Full** views.) Click **Copyright & Licensing** to open the area. It has two parts:

* **Copyright** – the copyright statement. PTXprint fills it in from the Paratext project settings. You can change it here. Click **Reload copyright from Paratext project** to get the Paratext text back.
* **License** – choose one of the Creative Commons licenses, **All Rights Reserved**, or type your own license.

PTXprint puts these texts into the front matter (for example on the title page back) through the variables `\zcopyright` and `\zlicense`. Some special codes work in both boxes: `(c)` becomes ©, `(r)` becomes ®, `(tm)` becomes ™, `~` is a non-breaking space, and `//` forces a new line.

## Layout Configuration

A **configuration** (or layout) is a named set of settings. One project can have many configurations, for example one for a draft and one for the final book. See the chapter about the main window for more about configurations and saving.

* **Name** – the list of saved configurations. Choose one to load its settings. You can also type a new name here and click **Save** to make a new configuration. Use only the letters a–z and A–Z, numbers, brackets `( )`, underscores `_` and hyphens `-`. No spaces.
* The **Save As** button (an icon next to the name) opens the **Save Current Configuration As...** dialog, where you type a name for a new configuration.
* The **lock** button locks or unlocks the configuration with a password.
* The **Copy configuration to other projects** button opens the **Copy Configuration To...** dialog. (Default and Full views.)
* **Delete** removes the selected configuration. For the **Default** configuration, this button is replaced by **Reset**.
* **Import Settings...** opens the **Import Settings** dialog, where you can bring settings in from a PDF, a ZIP archive, or another configuration. See the chapter "Importing settings". (Basic, Default and Full views.)
* **Notes** – an optional description of the configuration, for you and your team. (Basic, Default and Full views.)

When you choose another configuration in the **Name** list, PTXprint does **not** save the current one. Click **Save** first.

## What to Print

Choose one of three ways to say what goes into the PDF:

* **Single Book** – choose one book in the list. You can also type chapter numbers in **From Chapter** and **To** to print only part of the book. When you choose a new book, PTXprint sets the chapters to the whole book.
* **Portions or Multiple Books** – click **Select Multiple Books...** to choose books by clicking them, or type a list in the box. You can type book codes (`MAT MRK LUK JHN`), book ranges (`MAT-REV`) and references (`JHN 2:1-12`, `PSA 23; 100; 117`, `GEN 1:1-2:3`). Use the 3-letter USFM codes (for example `JHN`, not `John`). Press **Ctrl+B** to jump to this box.
* **Bible Module** – print a Paratext module (a .sfm file that lists passages to include). Click **Choose...** to select the module file. Click **Edit...** to see it on the **View+Edit** tab. (Bible Module is shown in the **Basic**, **Default** and **Full** views; **Edit...** in **Default** and **Full**.)

If you type in **From Chapter** or **To**, PTXprint changes to **Single Book**. If you type in the book list, PTXprint changes to **Portions or Multiple Books**.

The FRT (front matter) book is not in the book lists. Set up the front matter on the **Peripherals** tab instead.

## Dialogs on this tab

### Save Current Configuration As...

Opens when you click the **Save As** button. Type a name in **Configuration Name** and click **OK**. PTXprint makes a new configuration with a copy of the current settings, saves it, and changes to it. The **OK** button stays greyed out until the name is valid. PTXprint shows a message below the box if the name has spaces or special characters, or if a configuration with that name already exists.

Tip: Click **Save** before you use **Save As...**. Then the new configuration starts from your latest settings.

### Lock/Unlock Configuration

Opens when you click the **lock** button. Locking protects a configuration so that nobody changes or deletes it by mistake.

* **To lock:** type a password (up to 16 characters) and click **OK**. PTXprint saves the configuration and then locks it. The lock icon changes, and dots appear in the box next to the name.
* **To unlock:** click the lock button again, type the same password, and click **OK**. If the password is wrong, nothing happens.
* While a configuration is locked, **Save**, **Delete** and **Notes** are greyed out, and PTXprint does not save changes (not even when you print). You can still try out settings and print, but the changes are not kept.
* You cannot lock the **Default** configuration.

Note: if you click **Cancel** while the configuration is not locked, PTXprint may still lock it, with an empty password. To unlock it, click the lock button, leave the password box empty and click **OK**.

### Copy Configuration To...

Opens when you click the **Copy configuration to other projects** button. Use it when several projects need the same layout (for example, a series of New Testaments in related languages).

1. Click the projects that should receive a copy of the current configuration. The current project is shown in black and cannot be chosen. The **Recent** list at the bottom shows your selection, and remembers your last 10 selections.
2. Choose what to do if a target project already has a configuration with the same name:
   * **Do NOT Replace Existing Config** – skip those projects. Use this the first time you copy.
   * **Merge Configurations From Both** – combine the two. Settings that were changed in the target project since the first copy are kept.
   * **Overwrite With Recent Changes** – settings that were changed in this (source) project replace the target settings.
3. Click **OK**.

PTXprint copies the saved files of the configuration: the settings, the styles, the changes and TeX files, and the front matter. Adjust lists (paragraph adjustments) are not copied, because they belong to one text. Click **Save** before you copy, so that the copy has your latest settings.

### Select Books To Export to PDF

Opens when you click **Select Multiple Books...**. Each book in the project is a button. Click a button to select or unselect that book. Hold **Shift** and click another book to select or unselect all books between the two. The buttons at the side select groups: **All Books**, **Old Testament**, **New Testament**, **Deuterocanon**, **Extra Material**, **Toggle Books** (reverse the selection), and **Reset All** (unselect all). Click **OK**. PTXprint puts the books in the normal Bible order in the book list. You can then change the order in the list by typing, if needed.

### Import Scripture...

Opens when you choose **Import...** at the end of the **Project** list. There are two ways to get a text:

* **Install BSB** – installs the Berean Standard Bible, a public-domain English Bible that comes with PTXprint. It is good for practice and as a second text in a diglot.
* **Step 1 – Step 3** – install a Scripture text bundle (.zip):
  1. Download a bundle from the **Primary DBL site** (Digital Bible Library – you must log in) or the **Open.Bible site**. Choose a bundle that has the text (not only audio). The USX format is best.
  2. Click **Locate...** and choose the .zip file.
  3. Check the project name in **Assign a Name for the Project** and click **OK**.

PTXprint creates the new project in a folder called `_PTXprint` inside your Paratext projects folder, and opens it.

### Please Confirm...

PTXprint asks you to confirm before something that cannot be undone:

* **"You are about to REMOVE this Configuration"** – appears when you click **Delete**. Click **Yes** to delete the configuration, or **No** to keep it.
* **"You are about to CREATE a diglot (or polyglot) configuration"** – appears when you turn on a diglot. PTXprint suggests that you first use **Save As...** to make a new configuration for the diglot.

## Common tasks

### Start a new publication from an existing configuration

1. In **Project**, choose the project.
2. In **Name**, choose the configuration that is closest to what you want.
3. Click **Save** (so that the latest settings are on disk).
4. Click the **Save As** button. Type a new name (for example `NT_A5`) and click **OK**.
5. Now change the settings. The old configuration stays as it was.

### Print one book, or part of a book

1. Click **Single Book**.
2. Choose the book in the list.
3. To print only some chapters, type the first chapter in **From Chapter** and the last chapter in **To**.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

### Print several books, or selected passages

1. Click **Select Multiple Books...**.
2. Click the books you want (or click **New Testament**), then click **OK**.
3. Or type in the book list, for example `MAT-ACT` or `PSA 23; 100; 117 LUK 15:11-32`.
4. Click **Print (Make PDF)**.

### Protect a finished configuration

1. Choose the configuration in **Name** (not **Default**).
2. Click the **lock** button.
3. Type a password and click **OK**. Remember the password.

### Use the same layout for another project

1. Click **Save**.
2. Click the **Copy configuration to other projects** button. (Default or Full view.)
3. Click the target project(s).
4. Choose **Do NOT Replace Existing Config** and click **OK**.
5. In **Project**, choose the target project and check the copied configuration.

### Set or correct the copyright statement

1. Change to the **Default** or **Full** view if needed.
2. Click **Copyright & Licensing** to open it.
3. Type the copyright text (type `(c)` for ©), or click **Reload copyright from Paratext project**.
4. Choose or type the **License**.

### Get a text to practise with

1. Open the **Project** list and choose **Import...** (the last item).
2. Click **Install BSB**.
3. PTXprint installs and opens the BSB project.

### Delete a configuration that you do not need

1. Choose it in **Name**.
2. Click **Delete**, then **Yes**.
3. Before you delete, copy any PDF files that you want to keep to another folder (click the **Open folder containing the PDF** button at the bottom of the window to find them).

## Common problems

### My recent changes were lost when I chose another configuration

**Cause:** Choosing another configuration in the **Name** list does not save the current one. **What to do:** Always click **Save** before you change configurations.

### The lock button is greyed out

**Cause:** The **Default** configuration cannot be locked. **What to do:** Use **Save As** to make a named configuration, then lock that one.

### I cannot save, and Delete and Notes are greyed out

**Cause:** The configuration is locked. **What to do:** Click the lock button and enter the password, or use **Save As** to make a new, unlocked copy.

### There is a Reset button instead of Delete

**Cause:** The **Default** configuration is selected. It cannot be deleted. **Reset** is shown instead. Be careful: **Reset** asks no question. It sets all settings back to the PTXprint defaults at once.

### The OK button in "Save Current Configuration As..." is greyed out

**Cause:** The name is empty, has spaces or special characters, or is already used. **What to do:** Read the message below the box. Use only letters a–z and A–Z, numbers, `(`, `)`, `_` and `-`.

### PTXprint says "Unknown book code"

**Cause:** The book list has a word that is not a 3-letter USFM book code (for example `John`). **What to do:** Use the codes, for example `JHN`, `MAT`, `1CO`.

### I cannot find the FRT book in the list

**Cause:** PTXprint does not list FRT as a book. **What to do:** Set up front matter on the **Peripherals** tab.

### The Primary DBL site and Open.Bible site links do not work

**Cause:** **Disable ALL Internet Use** is ticked on the **Advanced** tab. **What to do:** Untick it, or download the bundle another way and use **Locate...**.

### Copyright & Licensing or Copy configuration are missing, or Reset is greyed out

**Cause:** They are only available in the **Default** and **Full** views. **What to do:** Click **☰** › **View Level** › **Default View**.

## Settings reference: Basic tab

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

### Import Scripture... (dialog)

#### OK

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Explanation:**

Installs the bundle that you chose with **Locate...**, using the name in **Assign a Name for the Project**, and opens the new project. It is greyed out until the name is valid and not already used.

*(Internal ID: `btn_dbl_ok`)*

#### Cancel

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Explanation:**

Closes the dialog without installing anything. PTXprint goes back to the project that was open before.

*(Internal ID: `btn_dbl_cancel`)*

#### Install BSB

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> The Berean Standard Bible is a Public Domain English Bible. It is bundled with PTXprint but needs to be installed in your Projects folder.
>
> This is a good training project and can also be used in diglots.

#### Locate...

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Locate DBL bundle
- **View level:** Basic, Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> After downloading a scripture text bundle (.zip) file you need to tell PTXprint where the .zip file is located so that it can install it as a special resource project.

**Explanation:**

Opens a file chooser in the `Bundles` folder of your Paratext projects folder. Choose the .zip file that you downloaded. PTXprint then shows the file name and suggests a project name from the bundle (adding a number if that name is already used). Shortcut: **Alt+O**.

*(Internal ID: `btn_locateDBLbundle`)*

#### Step 3 Assign a Name for the Project

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Text box
- **Description:** Assign a name to a DBL bundle
- **View level:** Basic, Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> PTXprint will create this project within a subfolder called '_PTXprint'. Use 8 characters or less for the new project name. Do not use the name of an existing Project.

**Explanation:**

The short name (ID) of the new project. PTXprint suggests one from the bundle. Change it if you want. Use 8 characters or fewer, with no spaces or special characters, and do not use the name of a project you already have. A message appears below the box if the name cannot be used.

*(Internal ID: `t_DBLprojName`)*

#### Primary DBL site

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Link
- **Description:** Visit the Digital Bible Library to download a DBL Scripture bundle
- **View level:** Basic, Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> There are hundreds of Scripture bundles available at the Digital Bible Library website which you may download and use in a publication. You must log in to the site in order to access resources.
>
> Use resources which contain the text (not just the audio) and preferably select the USX download option.
>
> Note: If this option is disabled, it is due to the "Disable ALL Internet Use" option which has been set on the General section of the Advanced tab.

**Explanation:**

Opens the Digital Bible Library website in your browser. You need a DBL login to download bundles. Choose a text bundle (not audio only), preferably in USX format. Greyed out when **Disable ALL Internet Use** is ticked on the **Advanced** tab.

*(Internal ID: `lb_DBLdownloads`)*

#### Open.Bible site

- **Where:** Import Scripture... (dialog)
- **Type:** Link
- **Description:** Visit the Open.Bible site to download a Scripture bundle
- **View level:** Basic, Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> There are hundreds of Scripture bundles at the Open.Bible website which you may download and use in a publication.
>
> Use resources which contain the text (not just the audio) and preferably select the USX download option.
>
> Note: If this option is disabled, it is due to the "Disable ALL Internet Use" option which has been set on the General section of the Advanced tab.
>
> If you don't already have a Scripture Text Bundle, then you can download a USX or USFM text bundle from an online scripture repository.

**Explanation:**

Opens the Open.Bible website in your browser, where you can download openly licensed Scripture bundles. Choose a text bundle, preferably USX. Greyed out when **Disable ALL Internet Use** is ticked on the **Advanced** tab.

*(Internal ID: `lb_openBible`)*

### Copy Configuration To... (dialog)

#### OK

- **Where:** Copy Configuration To... (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Explanation:**

Copies the current configuration to all selected projects, using the option you chose (Do NOT Replace, Merge, or Overwrite). The copy uses the saved files, so click **Save** in the main window before you open this dialog.

*(Internal ID: `btn_mps_ok`)*

#### Cancel

- **Where:** Copy Configuration To... (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Explanation:**

Closes the dialog. Nothing is copied.

*(Internal ID: `btn_mps_cancel`)*

#### Recent

- **Where:** Copy Configuration To... (dialog)
- **Type:** Drop-down list
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Shows selected target projects. Pick a previous selection from the dropdown, or select projects in the grid above.

**Explanation:**

Shows the names of the projects that you selected in the grid. You can also type project names here, separated by spaces, or choose an earlier selection from the list. PTXprint remembers your last 10 selections. This is useful when you copy to the same group of projects again and again.

*(Internal ID: `ecb_mpsTargets`)*

#### Do NOT Replace Existing Config

- **Where:** Copy Configuration To... (dialog)
- **Type:** Radio button
- **Description:** Copy Config: Do NOT Replace Existing Config
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Selecting this option will prevent any changes overwriting an existing configuration of the same name in the target project(s).
>
> This option is usually used when copying a configuration to other projects for the first time.

**Explanation:**

Copies the configuration only to projects that do **not** already have a configuration with this name. Projects that already have it are left unchanged. This is the safest choice, and the right choice the first time.

*(Internal ID: `r_copyConfig_noReplace`)*

#### Merge Configurations From Both

- **Where:** Copy Configuration To... (dialog)
- **Type:** Radio button
- **Description:** Copy Config: MERGE Configurations From Both
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Selecting this option will MERGE the settings from the source configuration with the identically named configuration in the target project. Any changes that were made to the target project's configuration since it was first shared will be kept (i.e. modified target settings are retained if there is a clash of settings).

**Explanation:**

For projects that already have a configuration with this name, PTXprint combines the two. When a setting was changed in the target project after the first copy, the target's value is kept. Other settings are updated from this project.

*(Internal ID: `r_copyConfig_merge`)*

#### Overwrite With Recent Changes

- **Where:** Copy Configuration To... (dialog)
- **Type:** Radio button
- **Description:** Copy Config: OVERWRITE With Recent Changes
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Selecting this option will REPLACE (or overwrite) any settings in the identically named configuration in the target project IF those settings were changed in the source project since the configuration was first shared. (i.e. if both source and target projects modified a setting, then the source project's setting will "win").

**Explanation:**

For projects that already have a configuration with this name, settings that were changed in this (source) project replace the values in the target. Use it when this project is the "master" layout for a group of projects.

*(Internal ID: `r_copyConfig_overwrite`)*

#### Cancel

- **Where:** Lock/Unlock Configuration (dialog)
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Explanation:**

This is the **Cancel** button of the Lock/Unlock dialog. Note: if the configuration is not locked, clicking it may lock the configuration with an empty password. To undo this, open the dialog again, leave the box empty and click **OK**.

#### Enter Password

- **Where:** Lock/Unlock Configuration (dialog)
- **Type:** Text box
- **Description:** Enter password for config
- **View level:** All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Enter a password of up to 16 characters to lock/unlock this saved configuration.

**Explanation:**

Type the password here. PTXprint does not store the password itself, only a coded form of it. If you forget the password, you cannot unlock the configuration in PTXprint, so keep it somewhere safe.
