# Peripherals tab (front and back matter)

## What this tab is for

The **Peripherals** tab controls everything that is printed **around** the Scripture text:

* the **front matter** – the pages before the Scripture text, such as the title page, the
  copyright page and the table of contents;
* the **back matter** – pages after the Scripture text, such as maps and the colophon;
* a **cover** for the book;
* ready-made PDF files that you want to add at the front or at the back.

Come here when you want a title page, a table of contents, a copyright statement, maps or a
cover. The words on these pages are written in the front matter. You edit the front matter on
the **View+Edit** tab. The special codes that you can use there (`\zcopyright`, `\ztoc`,
`\zvar` and others) are explained in the **View+Edit** tab chapter. This chapter explains the
settings that turn these parts on and off, and the table of **variables** (the values that
PTXprint puts into the front matter, such as the main title).

**View levels:** In the **Basic** view this tab shows only **Table of Contents**, **Local
Front Matter** and the variables table. All other settings on this tab are only shown in the
**Default** and **Full** views. When one of the main options on this tab is turned on, the
name of the tab is shown in a different colour, so you can see that the tab is in use.

## Cover

PTXprint can make a cover for the book: a back cover, a spine (the narrow back edge of a
bound book) and a front cover, all on one wide page (the "cover spread"). PTXprint saves the
cover in its **own PDF file**. The file has the same name as the main PDF, with **_cover** at
the end. Printers usually print the cover on different paper, so they want it as a separate file.

* Tick **Create Cover Page** to make a cover each time you print.
* Click **Cover Wizard...** to design the cover step by step (see below).
* The four links **Back Cover**, **Spine**, **Front Cover** and **Cover Spread** open the
  matching style on the **Styles** tab. Each part of the cover is a sidebar (a box). There you
  can change its background colour, background picture, border and other box settings. Use
  **Cover Spread** for things that go across the whole cover, for example one picture behind
  the back, spine and front.

The text on each part of the cover comes from special sections of the front matter
(`coverfront`, `coverspine` and `coverback`, plus `coverwhole` for the whole spread). So the
cover needs **Local Front Matter**. If you untick **Local Front Matter**, PTXprint also unticks
**Create Cover Page** and shows a message about it. If the front matter has no cover sections,
no cover is made. The easiest way to create these sections is the **Cover Wizard**.

There is no separate Cover tab in this version of PTXprint. Use the **Cover Wizard** and the
four style links instead.

### The Cover Wizard

Click **Cover Wizard...** (you must tick **Create Cover Page** first). A window opens. The
steps are on the left and a preview of the whole cover is on the right. Use **Next** and
**Back** to move between the steps.

1. **Book and Spine Setup** – type the approximate number of pages. PTXprint fills this in
   from the last PDF if it can. Choose whether the book has a spine (most books with fewer than
   about 80 pages do not have spine text). If it has a spine, choose **Paperback** or
   **Hardcover**, and choose how to find the spine width: **Automatic** (from the paper
   weight in gsm or the paper thickness in µm) or **Manual** (type the width in mm). Ask your
   printer for the paper thickness if you can. Tick the right-to-left binding option for
   books in scripts such as Arabic or Hebrew, which open on the other side.
2. **Picture / decoration** – choose where the main picture goes (no picture, across the whole
   cover, front only, front and spine, back only, back and spine, or separate pictures for
   front and back). Choose the picture file, how it fits (stretch or crop), and its opacity.
   You can also add a decorative border to the front cover.
3. **Background** – white, or a solid colour behind everything. (Gradient shading is not
   available yet.)
4. **Front cover text** – type the title (you must type a title before you can go on). You can
   also add a subtitle, the language name and a picture. Move the position slider of each item
   to place it higher or lower on the front cover. You can also change its colour and size.
5. **Spine text** (only when the book has a spine) – choose what to show on the spine (title,
   subtitle, language name), its colour, size, direction and position. (The publisher name on
   the spine is not available yet.)
6. **Back cover** – add a short text (a "blurb"), an ISBN barcode and a logo, and choose
   where they go.
7. **Review** – check the summary and the preview, then click **Finish**.

When you click **Finish**, PTXprint:

* writes new cover sections into the front matter (this **replaces** any cover sections that
  were there before);
* changes the cover styles (background, border, picture, title colours and sizes);
* puts the title, subtitle, language name and ISBN into the variables **maintitle**,
  **subtitle**, **languagename** and **isbn** in the variables table on this tab.

**Cancel** closes the wizard without changing anything. PTXprint remembers your wizard
answers with the configuration, so you can open the wizard again later and make changes.

## Front Matter PDF(s) and Back Matter PDF(s)

Use these when part of the book already exists as a PDF file, for example a title page made in
another program, or a set of maps or an index made elsewhere.

* Tick **Front Matter PDF(s)** and click **Select...** to choose one or more PDF files that
  go **before** the Scripture text.
* Tick **Back Matter PDF(s)** and click **Select...** to choose PDF files that go **after**
  the Scripture text.

The names of the chosen files are shown next to the button. Hold the mouse over **Select...**
to see the full path of each file. The PDF pages must have the same page size as your
publication.

## Table of Contents

Tick **Table of Contents** to let PTXprint make a table of contents (a list of the books with
their page numbers). It is useful when you print several books.

* **Title** – the heading of the table of contents, for example "Contents" in your language.
* **Use \toc1 / \toc2 / \toc3** – each book in Paratext has up to three names: `\toc1` (the
  long name), `\toc2` (the short name) and `\toc3` (the abbreviation). Each name that you tick
  becomes one column in the table of contents. At least one must be ticked.
* **Leaders** – dots or a line between the book name and the page number.

Where does the table of contents appear?

* If **Local Front Matter** is **not** ticked, PTXprint makes its own contents page with your
  title before the Scripture text.
* If **Local Front Matter** is ticked, the table of contents appears where the front matter
  has the code `\ztoc|main\*` (see the **View+Edit** tab chapter). The BASIC front matter
  template already contains this code.

PTXprint can only know the page numbers after the text has been typeset. It therefore
typesets the publication more than once when you click **Print**. If **Quick Run** is ticked,
it typesets only once. Then the status line says "Rerun to fix: table of contents", and you
must click **Print** again.

## Local Front Matter

PTXprint does not print the FRT (front matter) book of your Paratext project directly. It
keeps its own copy for each configuration. You change this copy on the **View+Edit** tab. Tick
**Local Front Matter** to print it. The first time you tick it, PTXprint makes a simple front
matter for you (title page, copyright page and table of contents) if there is none yet.

* **Edit...** takes you to the **Front Matter** sub-tab of the **View+Edit** tab.
* **Force Page Break at each Periph** – each section of the front matter (title page,
  copyright page, preface …) starts on a new page. Leave it ticked unless you want short
  sections to share a page.
* **Suppress Blank Page Before Scripture Text** – normally the Scripture text starts on a
  right-hand page, and PTXprint adds a blank page when needed. Tick this to stop the blank page.
* **Use Peripheral Introductory Sections** – see below.

**Note:** When you tick **Local Front Matter**, PTXprint unticks **Colophon at End of
Publication**, because most front matter already has a copyright page. When you untick
**Local Front Matter**, PTXprint ticks the colophon again (and turns off the cover). Check
these two settings after you change one of them.

### Use Peripheral Introductory Sections

Some projects have an INT (introductions) book in Paratext, with sections such as an
introduction to the Old Testament or to the Gospels. Each section starts with a `\periph`
line that has an id. Tick **Use Peripheral Introductory Sections** to make PTXprint put each
section in front of the first book of its group. The ids that PTXprint knows are:

| id | Placed before |
|---|---|
| `intbible` | the first book of the Bible |
| `intot` | the first Old Testament book |
| `intpent` | the first book of the Pentateuch (GEN–DEU) |
| `inthistory` | the first history book (JOS–EST) |
| `intpoetry` | the first poetry book (JOB–SNG) |
| `intprophesy` | the first book of the prophets (ISA–MAL) |
| `intdc` | the first Deuterocanon book |
| `intnt` | the first New Testament book |
| `intgospels` | the first Gospel (MAT–JHN) |
| `intepistles` | the first letter of Paul (ROM–PHM) |
| `intletters` | the first of the other letters (HEB–REV) |

The section is only printed when a book of that group is in the list of books to print.
**Force Page Break at each Periph** also decides whether these sections start on a new page.

## Maps

* **Add Maps...** opens the **Add Map** dialog. There you choose map pictures, and PTXprint
  writes one page for each map into a map book (usually XXM). This dialog is explained in the
  **Pictures** tab chapter.
* **Include Maps** adds the map book to the list of books to print (and changes the **Basic**
  tab to **Multiple Books** if needed). Untick it to take the map book out of the list again.
  PTXprint saves the configuration when you change this setting.
* **Edit...** shows the map book on the **View+Edit** tab. Nothing happens if there is no
  map book yet.

## Colophon at End of Publication

A colophon is a short text at the very end of the book, for example the copyright, the
licence and the picture credits. Tick **Colophon at End of Publication** to show the text box.
PTXprint prints the colophon after the end of the last book.

* Type the colophon in the **Colophon Text** box. You can use USFM markers such as `\pc`
  (centred paragraph) and the special codes `\zcopyright`, `\zlicense` and
  `\zimagecopyrights` (see the **View+Edit** tab chapter).
* The reset button below the box puts back the standard colophon (copyright, licence, a blank
  line and the picture credits). For a diglot it also adds the copyright of the second
  language. Anything you typed is replaced.
* **Force Page Break Before Colophon** puts the colophon on a new page at the end, instead
  of under the last lines of the last book.

The picture credits (`\zimagecopyrights`) need the page numbers of the pictures. Click
**Print** a second time to get correct picture credits.

## Variables and Values

This table lists the **variables** used in the front matter (and in the colophon and cover).
A variable is a place-holder such as `\zvar|maintitle\*`. When you print, PTXprint puts the
value from this table in its place. The values are saved with the configuration. So two
configurations can use the same kind of front matter with different titles.

The table has three columns:

* **Pub** – tick this to make the variable a field of each publication on the
  **Publications** tab. Then each publication can have its own value (for example its own
  title). **maintitle** and **subtitle** are always used there.
* **Name** – the name of the variable. You cannot change it here.
* **Value** – click the value to change it. Press Enter to keep the new value.

Buttons:

* **Rescan peripheral variables** looks for all `\zvar|...\*` codes in the front matter and adds
  any missing ones to the table with the value `<Type Value Here>`. It saves the front matter
  first.
* **Add** asks for the name of a new variable. Use only letters, numbers and hyphens, and no
  spaces (for example `printedby` or `maintitlefr`).
* **Del** deletes the selected variables.

The variable `toctitle` is special: it always uses the **Title** of the **Table of Contents**,
so it is not in this table.

## Common tasks

### Add a title page and a copyright page

1. On the **Basic** tab, check the copyright and licence statements.
2. On the **Peripherals** tab, tick **Local Front Matter**. PTXprint makes a simple front
   matter if there is none.
3. In the **Variables and Values** table, click the value of **maintitle** and type the
   title. Do the same for **subtitle** and any other variables.
4. Click **Print**.

To change the layout of these pages, click **Edit...** (see the **View+Edit** tab chapter).

### Add a table of contents

1. On the **Basic** tab, choose **Multiple Books** and the books to print.
2. On the **Peripherals** tab, tick **Table of Contents**.
3. Type the **Title**, for example "Contents" in your language.
4. Tick the book names to use (**\toc1**, **\toc2**, **\toc3**) and choose the **Leaders**.
5. If **Local Front Matter** is ticked, make sure that the front matter contains
   `\ztoc|main\*` (the BASIC template has it).
6. Click **Print**. If the status line asks you to rerun, click **Print** again.

### Make a cover

1. Tick **Local Front Matter** (a cover needs it).
2. Tick **Create Cover Page**.
3. Click **Cover Wizard...**, go through the steps and click **Finish**.
4. Click **Print**. The cover is saved as a separate PDF whose name ends with **_cover**.
5. To fine-tune colours, borders or pictures, click **Front Cover**, **Spine**, **Back Cover**
   or **Cover Spread** and change the style on the **Styles** tab.

### Add an existing PDF before or after the Scripture text

1. Tick **Front Matter PDF(s)** (or **Back Matter PDF(s)**).
2. Click **Select...** and choose one or more PDF files.
3. Click **Print**.

### Put the copyright and picture credits at the end of the book

1. Tick **Colophon at End of Publication**.
2. If the box is empty, click the reset button under the box to get the standard text.
3. Tick **Force Page Break Before Colophon** if you want it on its own page.
4. Click **Print**, and then **Print** again, so that the picture credits are correct.

### Add your own variable

1. Click **Add**, type a name such as `printedby`, and click **OK**.
2. Click the **Value** of the new row and type the text.
3. On the **View+Edit** tab, put `\zvar|printedby\*` in the front matter where the text
   should appear.

### Insert book group introductions from the INT book

1. In Paratext, give each section of the INT book an id, for example
   `\periph New Testament Introduction|id="intnt"`.
2. On the **Peripherals** tab, tick **Use Peripheral Introductory Sections**.
3. Print a set of books that includes a book of that group (for example MAT for `intnt`).

## Common problems

**The cover is not created.**
Check that **Local Front Matter** and **Create Cover Page** are both ticked. The front matter
must contain cover sections. Run the **Cover Wizard** and click **Finish** to create them.
Remember that the cover is in a **separate** PDF file (name ending in **_cover**), not in the
main PDF.

**Create Cover Page became unticked by itself.**
You unticked **Local Front Matter**. A cover cannot be made without it. Tick both again.

**The Cover Wizard button is greyed out.**
Tick **Create Cover Page** first.

**The Finish button in the Cover Wizard is greyed out.**
You must type a title in the front cover step, and you must be on the last (review) step.

**My hand-made changes to the cover text disappeared.**
**Finish** in the Cover Wizard replaces the cover sections of the front matter. Make the
changes again on the **View+Edit** tab after you use the wizard.

**The colophon disappeared after I turned on Local Front Matter.**
PTXprint unticks **Colophon at End of Publication** when you tick **Local Front Matter**. Tick
the colophon again if you want both.

**The table of contents is empty or the page numbers are wrong.**
Click **Print** again (especially if **Quick Run** is ticked). If **Local Front Matter** is
ticked, the front matter must contain `\ztoc|main\*`. Check that at least one of
**\toc1**/**\toc2**/**\toc3** is ticked and that the books have those markers in Paratext.

**A book is missing from the table of contents.**
The book has no text for the ticked `\toc` markers. Add the `\toc1` (or `\toc2`, `\toc3`)
line to the book in Paratext, or tick another `\toc` option.

**The picture credits in the colophon or front matter are wrong or empty.**
Click **Print** a second time. PTXprint needs a first run to find the page of each picture.

**A variable prints as "<Type Value Here>".**
Click its **Value** in the **Variables and Values** table and type the text.

**A variable I deleted came back.**
**Rescan peripheral variables** (and generating front matter) adds every variable that is used
in the front matter. Remove the `\zvar` code from the front matter first, then delete the row.

**There is a blank page before the Scripture text.**
PTXprint starts the Scripture text on a right-hand page. Tick **Suppress Blank Page Before
Scripture Text** if you do not want this.

**The maps are printed although I do not want them.**
Untick **Include Maps**. This takes the map book out of the list of books to print.

**Most of the settings on this tab are missing.**
You are using the **Basic** view. Change to the **Default** or **Full** view.

## Settings reference: Peripherals tab (front and back matter)

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

### Peripherals tab

#### Create Cover Page

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Create an outer Cover
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Create a cover (back, spine and front) as a separate PDF file ending in _cover.pdf. Needs Local Front Matter. Use the Cover Wizard... to design it.

**Explanation:**

Makes a cover each time you print, and saves it as a separate PDF whose name ends with
**_cover**. The cover pages are taken out of the main PDF. It needs **Local Front Matter**,
because the cover text is kept in cover sections of the front matter; if you untick **Local
Front Matter**, this is unticked too. Use **Cover Wizard...** to create the cover sections.

*(Internal ID: `c_makeCoverPage` · Config key: `cover/makecoverpage`)*

#### Cover Wizard...

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Generate Cover (Basic settings to create a cover)
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Only available when:** “Create Cover Page” is selected
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Creating a cover from nothing takes a lot of effort. This tool enables you to create various kinds of covers which can easily be enhanced.

**Explanation:**

Opens the Cover Wizard, which leads you through 6 or 7 steps (page count and spine, pictures,
background, front text, spine text, back cover, review) with a live preview. **Finish** writes
the cover sections into the front matter, sets the cover styles, and fills in the
**maintitle**, **subtitle**, **languagename** and **isbn** variables. Any cover sections that
were in the front matter before are replaced. Greyed out until **Create Cover Page** is ticked.

*(Internal ID: `btn_coverGenerate`)*

#### Back Cover

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Link
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the Back Cover.

**Explanation:**

Opens the **Styles** tab at the style of the back cover box. Change its background colour,
background picture, border or padding there. The text of the back cover is in the `coverback`
section of the front matter.

*(Internal ID: `lb_style_cat:coverback|esb`)*

#### Spine

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Link
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the Spine.

**Explanation:**

Opens the **Styles** tab at the style of the spine box (background, border, text direction).
The spine text is in the `coverspine` section of the front matter.

*(Internal ID: `lb_style_cat:coverspine|esb`)*

#### Front Cover

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Link
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the Front Cover.

**Explanation:**

Opens the **Styles** tab at the style of the front cover box. Use it to change the front
background colour or picture, or the border. The front cover text is in the `coverfront`
section of the front matter.

*(Internal ID: `lb_style_cat:coverfront|esb`)*

#### Cover Spread

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Link
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the whole Cover Spread (the background behind the back, spine and front).

**Explanation:**

Opens the **Styles** tab at the style for the whole cover spread (back, spine and front
together). It is the bottom layer: the back, spine and front boxes are placed on top of it.
Use it for a background colour or one picture that goes across the whole cover.

*(Internal ID: `lb_style_cat:coverwhole|esb`)*

#### Front Matter PDF(s)

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Enable import of front matter PDF(s)
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> One or more previously created PDF file(s) can be included BEFORE the scripture material being typeset. If more than one file is selected, then these will appear in alphabetical order.
>
> If you are creating an electronic publication and want to add a fancy (colour) cover, then consider designing a cover using the online Canva.com tool.

**Explanation:**

Adds ready-made PDF pages before the Scripture text (and before the local front matter).
Use it for pages made in another program. The pages should have the same page size as the
publication. **Select...** is greyed out until this box is ticked.

*(Internal ID: `c_inclFrontMatter` · Config key: `project/ifinclfrontpdf`)*

#### Select...

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Select front matter PDF(s) to import
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Only available when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)” is selected
- **This tab/section appears when:** “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents   Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

**Explanation:**

Choose one or more PDF files. Hold the Ctrl key to choose several. The file names are then
shown next to the button, and the full paths are shown when you hold the mouse over the
button. To change the list, click the button again and choose all the files you want.

*(Internal ID: `btn_selectFrontPDFs` · Config key: `project/frontincludes`)*

#### Table of Contents   Title

- **Where:** Peripherals tab
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Enable table of contents
- **View level:** Default and Full views

# Publications tab

## What this tab is for

Sometimes you want to make several similar books from one project with the same design. For
example: one PDF for each Gospel, or a New Testament and a separate book of Psalms, each with
its own title. The **Publications** tab lets you do this without making a new configuration
for each book.

A **publication** here means: this configuration, printed with

* its own list of books, and
* its own values for some of the variables of the front matter (for example the main title
  and the subtitle).

All other settings (page size, fonts, layout, front matter, cover and so on) come from the
current configuration. You make a list of publications, tick the ones you want, and click
**Print Selected**. PTXprint then makes one PDF for each ticked publication.

This tab is only shown in the **Default** and **Full** views.

## The list of publications

The list has three columns:

* **Print** – tick the publications that you want to print. The checkbox in the column
  heading ticks or unticks all publications at once.
* **Publication ID / Field** – on the first (bold) line of each publication, this is the name
  of the publication. Under it are the names of its fields (variables).
* **Books / Value** – on the bold line, the books to print. Under it, the value of each field
  for this publication.

Click the small arrow beside a publication (or double-click its line) to show or hide its
fields. **Expand All** and **Collapse All** do this for all publications.

To change a value, click it, type the new text and press Enter. You can change:

* the **name** of a publication (the bold text in the second column). Each name must be
  different. The name is also used in the name of the PDF file, so keep it short and simple;
* the **books** of a publication (the bold text in the third column);
* the **value** of each field.

You cannot change the names of the fields here. They come from the variables table on the
**Peripherals** tab (see below).

### The books

Type the books in the same way as on the **Basic** tab, for example:

* `MRK` – one book;
* `RUT JON` – several books;
* `MAT-JHN` – a range of books;
* `JHN 1-5` – some chapters of one book.

You can also type the name of a module file (a file that lists which parts of the text to
print). If PTXprint cannot understand the books, the text turns red. Hold the mouse over it
to see what is wrong.

### The fields

Each publication always has the fields **maintitle** and **subtitle**. To add more fields,
go to the **Peripherals** tab and tick **Pub** beside a variable in the **Variables and
Values** table. The variable is then added to every publication. Untick **Pub** to remove it
again (except for **maintitle** and **subtitle**).

When you print a publication, PTXprint uses its values instead of the values on the
**Peripherals** tab. This only changes that one PDF. The values on the **Peripherals** tab are
not changed. For this to work, the front matter (or the cover) must use the variables, for
example `\zvar|maintitle\*` on the title page.

If the book has a cover with a spine, there is also a **pagecount** field. It holds the number
of pages of that publication. PTXprint uses it to work out the width of the spine for that
publication's cover.

## The buttons

* **Add** makes a new publication from the current settings: the books chosen on the
  **Basic** tab, and the current values of the variables. Its name is the main title (or
  "New publication"). It is ticked for printing.
* **Duplicate** makes a copy of the highlighted publication, called "Copy of ...". This is
  the quickest way to make a set of similar publications: duplicate, then change the name,
  books and title.
* **Delete** removes the highlighted publication, after asking you.
* **Expand All** / **Collapse All** show or hide the fields of all publications.
* **Print Selected** prints every ticked publication.

The line at the bottom shows how many publications are ticked, and how many have books that
PTXprint cannot understand.

## Printing the publications

When you click **Print Selected**, PTXprint:

1. saves the configuration (including the list of publications);
2. checks the books of each ticked publication. If some are wrong, it asks if it should
   print the others and skip these;
3. prints the publications in the background, several at the same time. The number at the
   same time is set by **Maximum parallel processes** on the **Advanced** tab;
4. opens the folder with the PDFs when all are finished.

Each PDF is named after the project, the configuration and the publication name. The PDFs are
not shown in the PDF preview. Open them from the folder.

While the publications are printing, **Print Selected** is greyed out.

The list of publications is saved with the configuration.

## Common tasks

### Make one PDF for each Gospel

1. On the **Peripherals** tab, tick **Local Front Matter** and make sure the title page uses
   `\zvar|maintitle\*` (the standard front matter does).
2. On the **Publications** tab, click **Add**.
3. Click the bold name and type `Matthew`. Click the books and type `MAT`.
4. Open the publication and click the value of **maintitle**. Type the title of Matthew in
   your language.
5. Click **Duplicate**. Change the copy's name to `Mark`, its books to `MRK`, and its title.
6. Do the same for Luke and John.
7. Tick all four and click **Print Selected**.

### Give each publication its own value for another variable

1. On the **Peripherals** tab, in the **Variables and Values** table, tick **Pub** beside the
   variable (for example **isbn**).
2. On the **Publications** tab, open each publication and type its value.

### Print only some of the publications

1. Untick all publications with the checkbox in the **Print** column heading.
2. Tick the ones you want.
3. Click **Print Selected**.

### Remove a publication

1. Click the publication (or one of its fields).
2. Click **Delete**, then confirm.

## Common problems

**Print Selected is greyed out.**
No publication is ticked, or PTXprint is still printing the last set.

**Duplicate and Delete are greyed out.**
Click a publication in the list first.

**The books are shown in red.**
PTXprint cannot understand the list of books. Hold the mouse over the red text to see the
problem. Use the 3-letter book codes, separated by spaces, for example `GEN EXO`.

**"None of the selected publications can be printed".**
All ticked publications have no books or wrong books. Correct the books.

**All the PDFs have the same title.**
The front matter does not use the variable, or it uses a different variable. Check that the
title page contains `\zvar|maintitle\*` (see the **View+Edit** tab chapter), and that
**Local Front Matter** is ticked on the **Peripherals** tab.

**A variable is not in the publications.**
Tick **Pub** beside the variable on the **Peripherals** tab.

**"A publication called ... already exists".**
Each publication needs a different name. Choose another name.

**The Publications tab is missing.**
You are using the **Basic** or **Minimal** view. Change to **Default** or **Full**.

## Settings reference: Publications tab

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

### Publications tab

#### Add

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Add a new publication, filled in from the current configuration: the books chosen on the Basic tab, and the title, subtitle and other publishable \zvars from the Peripherals tab.

**Explanation:**

Adds a new publication, ticked for printing. Its books are the books currently chosen on the
**Basic** tab (or the module, or the chapter range), and its fields get the current values of
the variables from the **Peripherals** tab. If a publication with that name already exists,
PTXprint adds a number, for example "(2)".

*(Internal ID: `btn_pubAdd`)*

#### Duplicate

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Make a complete copy of the highlighted publication, named 'Copy of ...' (Click a publication first.)

**Explanation:**

Copies the highlighted publication with all its books and values. Use it to make a series of
similar publications quickly. Greyed out until you click a publication in the list.

*(Internal ID: `btn_pubDuplicate`)*

#### Delete

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Delete the highlighted publication (you will be asked to confirm). (Click a publication first.)

**Explanation:**

Removes the highlighted publication from the list after you confirm. It does not delete PDFs
that were already made. Greyed out until you click a publication.

*(Internal ID: `btn_pubDel`)*

#### Expand All

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Show the details of every publication.

**Explanation:**

Opens all publications so that you can see every field and value. Useful for checking all
titles before you print.

*(Internal ID: `btn_pubExpandAll`)*

#### Collapse All

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Hide the details of every publication.

**Explanation:**

Closes all publications so that you only see their names and books. Useful when the list is
long.

*(Internal ID: `btn_pubCollapseAll`)*

#### tv_publications

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Table
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Explanation:**

The list of publications. The bold line of each publication shows the **Print** checkbox, the
name and the books. The lines under it show the fields (variables) and their values for that
publication. Click a name, the books or a value to change it; press Enter to keep the change.
Books that PTXprint cannot understand are shown in red.

*(Internal ID: `tv_publications`)*

#### Print Selected

- **Where:** Publications tab
- **Type:** Button
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Save the configuration, then create a PDF for each ticked publication (in the background). The folder with the PDFs opens when they are finished.

**Explanation:**

Saves the configuration, then prints each ticked publication in the background (several at
the same time) and opens the folder with the new PDFs when all are done. Publications with
wrong books are skipped after asking you. Greyed out when nothing is ticked or while printing.

*(Internal ID: `btn_pubPrint`)*


# Finishing tab

## What this tab is for

The **Finishing** tab controls what happens to the PDF *after* the pages have been typeset. Come here when you are getting ready to send the book to a printer, or when you want to print it yourself as a folded booklet.

On this tab you can:

* choose the **PDF Output Format** that your printer asks for (for example CMYK or black and white);
* add **crop marks** and a **watermark** (such as the word "DRAFT");
* print the pages as a **booklet** (two or more pages on each sheet of paper, in the right order for folding);
* **compare** the new PDF with an older one, to see exactly what changed;
* keep older copies of the PDF, and store your settings inside the PDF.

The **Finishing** tab is shown in the **Default** and **Full** views. Some settings are only shown in the **Full** view. This is noted for each setting below.

Most settings on this tab do not change the layout of the text. They change the finished PDF file. You must click **Print** (make the PDF again) before a change is visible.

### Some print-shop words in simple terms

* **Trim size** – the size of the finished book page, after the printer cuts it. In PTXprint this is the **Page Size** on the **Layout** tab.
* **Crop marks** (also called trim marks) – thin lines in the corners, outside the page, that show the printer where to cut.
* **Bleed** – a picture or colour that goes right to the edge of the page. The printer needs it to go a little *past* the cut line (usually about 3 mm), so that no white strip shows if the cut is not exact.
* **RGB** – the colours used by screens (Red, Green, Blue).
* **CMYK** – the four inks used by most colour printing presses (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and blacK). Many printers ask for CMYK files.
* **Grayscale (B/W)** – only black ink, in shades of grey.
* **Spot colour** – one extra, ready-mixed ink (often a Pantone colour) used in addition to black, for example red for the words of Jesus or for headings.
* **PDF/X** – a type of PDF made for printing. It contains everything the printer needs (fonts, colour information) and nothing that could cause problems.
  * **PDF/X-1a** – the older, strict type. All colours must be CMYK (or grey/spot) and there may be no transparency (see-through effects). Many printing presses still ask for this.
  * **PDF/X-4** – the newer type. It allows RGB colours with colour profiles and transparency. Many modern printers and digital (print-on-demand) printers accept it.
* **PDF/A** – a type of PDF made for keeping documents for a very long time (archiving).
* **Imposition** – arranging several book pages on one large sheet of paper, so that after folding and cutting the pages come out in the right order.
* **Signature** – a group of sheets that are folded together and sewn or glued into the book as one unit.

If your printer gives you a list of requirements, read it carefully. Look for: trim size, bleed, crop marks (yes or no), colour (CMYK, grey, or RGB), and PDF type (PDF/X-1a or PDF/X-4). Then set these on the **Layout** tab and on this tab. If you are not sure, ask the printer for a sample "print-ready PDF specification".

## PDF Details

This area controls the type of PDF that PTXprint makes. (This area is shown in the **Default** and **Full** views. Some settings are only in the **Full** view.)

### PDF Output Format

Choose the format that matches how the book will be used:

* **Screen (Quickest)** – the normal choice while you are still working on the book. PTXprint makes the PDF directly, with no extra processing. Use this for checking and proof-reading.
* **Digital-RGB** – a PDF/X-4 file in RGB colours. Good for reading on screen, for sharing as an e-book, and for printing on an office or home printer.
* **Digital-CMYK (Transparency)** – a PDF/X-4 file for printers who want CMYK but can accept transparency.
* **Print-CMYK** – a PDF/X-1a file with all colours turned into CMYK. Use this for a commercial printing press that asks for PDF/X-1a or CMYK.
* **Print-Gray (B/W)** – a PDF/X-1a file in black and shades of grey only. Use this for a book printed only in black ink. Coloured text and pictures are turned into grey.
* **Print-Spot** – black plus one spot colour. Any colour close to the **Color Hue** you choose is printed with the spot ink; everything else is printed in black and grey. The **Color Hue** and **Tolerance (%)** settings are only active when you choose this format.

The formats other than **Screen** need extra processing after the PDF is made. This takes more time, especially when the book has many pictures. PTXprint shows a note in the status bar about this.

PTXprint adds a short ending to the PDF file name, so you can see which format a file has: **_RGB**, **_CMYK-Transparent**, **_CMYK**, **_BW** or **_Spot**. **Screen** adds nothing.

When you choose **Print-CMYK**, **Print-Gray** or **Print-Spot** and thumb tabs are turned on, PTXprint turns on **Only Show on Odd Pages** for the thumb tabs (on the **Tabs+Borders** tab), and tells you in the status bar.

### Other PDF settings

* **Crop Marks** adds cut lines around every page. To make room for them, PTXprint makes each PDF page larger by 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) on every side. Only turn this on if your printer asks for crop marks. Many print-on-demand printers do *not* want them.
* **Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept** keeps older copies of your PDF (with **_1**, **_2** … at the end of the name). You need at least 1 to use **Compare PDFs** with the previous version.
* **Include Config Settings Within PDF** stores your settings inside the PDF file. Later, you (or someone else) can load the settings back from this PDF, using **Import Settings**.
* **Archive (PDF/A-4)** makes a PDF that is better for long-term storage. (Only in the **Full** view.)
* **Extract Color Inserts** and **Extra XDV Processing** are special tools. (Only in the **Full** view.)
* **Apply Watermark PDF** puts a PDF (for example "DRAFT") on every page.

## Booklet Pagination

This area lets you print several book pages on one larger sheet of paper, arranged so that you can fold the sheets into a booklet. This is called imposition. (This area is shown in the **Basic**, **Default** and **Full** views. Some settings are only in the **Full** view.)

* **Pages Per Spread** – how many book pages go on *one side* of a sheet. **1-up (No booklet)** is the normal setting: one page per PDF page. **2-up** is a normal folded booklet: for example, A5 pages on A4 paper. **4-up** and **8-up** put more pages on bigger sheets, for printers who fold the sheet more than once.
* **Physical Paper Size** – the size of the sheet you will print on. For 2-up, it is normally twice the page size (A5 pages → A4 sheet).
* **Sheets Per Signature**, **Fold Cut Margin (mm)** and **Fold First** are for professional binding. (Only in the **Full** view.) Leave them at their starting values unless the printer tells you what to use.

When **Pages Per Spread** is more than 1-up:

* the signature settings become active;
* **Scale to fit** is greyed out;
* the **Finishing** tab label changes colour, to remind you that the PDF will be imposed;
* the PDF file name gets an extra ending, such as **_2up**;
* crop marks (if ticked) are drawn on the large sheet, not on each page.

When **Pages Per Spread** is **1-up**, you can tick **Scale to fit**. Then PTXprint enlarges or shrinks each page so that it fits the **Physical Paper Size**, centred on the sheet.

If the pages do not fit on the paper you chose, PTXprint shows a **Paper Size Error**. Choose a larger **Physical Paper Size** or a smaller number of pages per spread.

## Compare PDFs

This area makes a "diff" PDF that shows what changed between the new PDF and an older one. This is very useful after a late correction: you can quickly check that only the expected pages changed. (The two colour settings are only shown in the **Full** view. **Show Max Diff Pages** is shown in the **Default** and **Full** views.)

How it works:

1. PTXprint keeps a copy of the previous PDF (the file ending **_1.pdf**), as long as **Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept** is 1 or more.
2. When **Compare PDFs** is ticked and you click **Print**, PTXprint makes the new PDF and then compares it with the old one.
3. If it finds differences, it makes a file ending **_diff.pdf** and opens it. Added or moved text is shown in one colour; removed text or old positions in another colour.
4. If there are no differences, the status bar says **No differences found**.

By default PTXprint compares with the previous PDF (**Previous PDF (_1)**). Click **Select...** to compare with any other PDF instead, for example the PDF you sent for the last proof check.

## Common tasks

### Make a PDF for a commercial printer who asks for PDF/X-1a in CMYK

1. On the **Layout** tab, check that the **Page Size** is the trim size the printer wants.
2. On the **Finishing** tab, in the **PDF Details** area, set **PDF Output Format** to **Print-CMYK**.
3. Tick **Crop Marks** only if the printer asks for crop marks.
4. Make sure **Pages Per Spread** is **1-up (No booklet)**. Printers do their own imposition.
5. Click **Print**. The new PDF name ends with **_CMYK**.

### Make a black-and-white PDF for printing

1. On the **Finishing** tab, set **PDF Output Format** to **Print-Gray (B/W)**.
2. Click **Print**. All colours in text and pictures become shades of grey. The file name ends with **_BW**.

### Print an A5 booklet on A4 paper on an office printer

1. On the **Layout** tab, set the page size to A5.
2. On the **Finishing** tab, in **Booklet Pagination**, set **Pages Per Spread** to **2-up**.
3. Set **Physical Paper Size** to **210mm, 297mm (A4)**.
4. Click **Print**. The new PDF (ending **_2up**) has two pages side by side on each A4 sheet, in booklet order.
5. Print it double-sided. For 2-up, choose "flip on short edge" in your printer settings. Print one or two test sheets first.
6. Fold the stack of sheets in the middle and staple along the fold.

### Use a paper size that is not in the list

1. Click in the **Physical Paper Size** box and type the width and height, separated by a comma. For example: `203mm, 330mm`.
2. You can use mm or in.

### See what changed since the last PDF

1. On the **Finishing** tab, check that **Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept** is at least 1.
2. Tick **Compare PDFs** (or press Ctrl+R).
3. Make your corrections, then click **Print**.
4. The "diff" PDF opens and shows the changes in colour. Untick **Compare PDFs** when you are finished.

### Compare with an older proof, not just the last run

1. In the **Compare PDFs** area, click **Select...** and choose the older PDF.
2. Tick **Compare PDFs** and click **Print**.
3. To go back to comparing with the previous run, click **Select...** again and click **Cancel** in the file dialog.

### Put "DRAFT" on every page

1. In the **PDF Details** area, tick **Apply Watermark PDF**.
2. Click **Select...** next to it. PTXprint opens its own folder of watermarks. Choose the one that matches your page size (for example **A5-Draft.pdf**).
3. Click **Print**.

### Send your settings to someone else inside the PDF

1. Tick **Include Config Settings Within PDF** (it is ticked by default).
2. Click **Print** and send the PDF.
3. The other person can load your settings from that PDF using **Import Settings** (see the chapter on importing settings).

## Common problems

**The colours look different in the printed book from on screen.**
Screens use RGB. Printing presses use CMYK, which cannot show some bright colours. Choose **Print-CMYK** (or the format your printer asks for), click **Print**, and check the result before you send it. Ask the printer for a printed proof if colour is important.

**Making the PDF is now very slow.**
A **PDF Output Format** other than **Screen** needs extra processing, especially for pictures. While you are still editing, use **Screen (Quickest)**. Change to the final format only for the last PDF. Also, **Compare PDFs** adds time, because it renders the pages as images.

**The PDF pages are bigger than my page size.**
**Crop Marks** is ticked. Crop marks add 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) on each side of every page. Untick **Crop Marks** if the printer did not ask for them.

**The PDF is two pages per sheet, or the file name ends with _2up.**
**Pages Per Spread** is not set to **1-up (No booklet)**. Set it back to **1-up** for a normal PDF. Commercial printers almost always want single pages (1-up).

**I see a "Paper Size Error" message.**
The book pages do not fit on the **Physical Paper Size** with the chosen **Pages Per Spread**. Choose a larger sheet or fewer pages per spread.

**"Scale to fit" is greyed out.**
It only works with **1-up (No booklet)**. Set **Pages Per Spread** to **1-up**.

**"Sheets Per Signature", "Fold Cut Margin" and "Fold First" are greyed out or missing.**
They are only active when **Pages Per Spread** is 2-up or more, and they are only shown in the **Full** view.

**"Color Hue" and "Tolerance" are greyed out.**
They are only used for **Print-Spot**. Set **PDF Output Format** to **Print-Spot** first.

**Compare PDFs does not show anything, or says there is nothing to compare.**
There must be an older PDF to compare with. Check that **Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept** is at least 1, and click **Print** once without comparing, so that a previous copy exists. If you used **Select...**, check that the chosen file still exists.

**The watermark is missing or in the wrong place.**
The watermark PDF should have the same page size as your book. Choose a file that matches your page size. If the watermark file was moved or deleted, PTXprint warns you that it cannot find it. Click **Select...** again.

**The maps (or other insert pages) are missing from my PDF.**
**Extract Color Inserts** is ticked. These pages were saved as separate PDF files next to the main PDF. Untick it if you want them inside the main PDF.

**Thumb tabs now appear only on odd pages.**
When you chose **Print-CMYK**, **Print-Gray** or **Print-Spot**, PTXprint turned on **Only Show on Odd Pages** for thumb tabs. You can change it back on the **Tabs+Borders** tab.

## Settings reference: Finishing tab

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

### Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination

#### Physical Paper Size

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Drop-down list
- **Description:** Pagination: Physical paper size
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Choices:** 420mm, 594mm (A2); 297mm, 420mm (A3); 210mm, 297mm (A4); 17in, 22in (ANSI C); 11in, 17in (ANSI B); 8.5in, 11in (Letter); 353mm, 500mm (B3); 250mm, 353mm (B4); 176mm, 250mm (B5)

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> If the required size is not displayed, then just type the required page width and height separated by a comma.
>
> For example: 203mm, 330mm (Foolscap)
>
> This is the actual size of the sheet of paper on which multiple pages will be printed. For example, if printing an A5-sized booklet, the actual sheet of paper that you print on will be 2x the A5-sized page, which is an A4-sized sheet of paper.

**Explanation:**

The size of the paper that goes into the printer, not the size of the book page. It is only used when **Pages Per Spread** is 2-up or more, or when **Scale to fit** is ticked. For a 2-up booklet, choose a sheet that is twice the book page (A5 book → A4 sheet; Letter-half book → Letter sheet). You can type any size as "width, height", for example `203mm, 330mm`. If the pages do not fit, you get a **Paper Size Error** when you print.

*(Internal ID: `ecb_sheetSize` · Config key: `finishing/sheetsize`)*

#### Pages Per Spread

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Drop-down list
- **Description:** Pagination: Pages per spread (booklet printing)
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Choices:** 1-up (No booklet); 2-up; 4-up; 8-up

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> How many pages will be printed on one side of the physical paper?
>
> For example, for an A5-sized booklet, 2 pages will fit on each side, making a total of 4 pages on a single sheet.

**Explanation:**

**1-up (No booklet)** makes a normal PDF with one book page on each PDF page. This is what commercial and print-on-demand printers want. **2-up** makes a simple folded booklet that you can print yourself on double-sided paper. **4-up** and **8-up** are for sheets that are folded twice or three times, usually by a print shop. When this is more than 1-up, the PDF file name gets an ending like **_2up**, and the signature settings become active.

*(Internal ID: `fcb_pagesPerSpread` · Config key: `finishing/pgsperspread`)*

#### Scale to fit

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Pagination: Scale to fit
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Only available when Pages per Spread is 1-up. Enable this option to scale every page (up or down) so that it fits the Physical Paper Size (set on this tab), centred on the sheet.

**Explanation:**

Only active when **Pages Per Spread** is **1-up**. PTXprint enlarges or shrinks every page so that it fits the **Physical Paper Size**, and centres it on the sheet. Use it, for example, to print an A5 proof on A4 paper with larger text. The book layout does not change; only the final PDF is scaled.

*(Internal ID: `c_scaleToFit` · Config key: `finishing/scaletofit`)*

#### Sheets Per Signature

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Number box
- **Description:** Pagination: Sheets per signature (pages per form)
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> A signature is a collection of pages folded and bound together as a unit. A signature may be made up of multiple sheets.
>
> If unsure, leave this setting at 0 to indicate that the publication will not be bound using separate signatures.

**Explanation:**

How many sheets of paper are folded together into one signature (one group of pages in the book). 0 means the whole book is one group, like a stapled booklet. Only change this if your printer or binder tells you how many sheets they put in each signature. Only active when **Pages Per Spread** is 2-up or more.

*(Internal ID: `s_sheetsPerSignature` · Config key: `finishing/sheetsinsigntr`)*

#### Fold Cut Margin (mm)

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Number box
- **Description:** Pagination: Minimum fold cut margin
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> The minimum width of the area to be cut after folding of the signature. Measured in millimeters (mm).

**Explanation:**

Extra space (in mm) left at the folds of a signature, where the paper will be cut after folding. Only needed for 4-up and 8-up sheets that are folded and then trimmed. Use the value your printer gives you. Leave it at 0 for a simple 2-up booklet.

*(Internal ID: `s_foldCutMargin` · Config key: `finishing/foldcutmargin`)*

#### Fold First

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Pagination: Fold First
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> If you are imposing for a printer with a folding machine, then you want to fold first and then cut. This, for example makes a folded sheet that is part of a signature consist of two sets of sequential pages.

**Explanation:**

Changes the page order on the sheet to suit a print shop that folds the sheets first and cuts them after. Leave it unticked unless the printer asks for "fold first". Only active when **Pages Per Spread** is 2-up or more.

*(Internal ID: `c_foldFirst` · Config key: `finishing/foldfirst`)*

#### Create Cover as a Separate PDF

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
- **Type:** Checkbox (ticked by default)
- **Description:** Pagination: Create the cover as a stand-alone PDF
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> This option is only available if Create Cover is enabled on the Cover tab. Enable this option if you plan to print the outer (wrapper) cover separately from the book's content. This is often the case if cardstock, or a colour cover is used.

**Explanation:**

Most printers print the cover on different paper (thicker card, or colour) from the inside pages, so they want the cover as its own PDF file. When PTXprint makes a cover, it saves the cover pages in a separate PDF whose name ends with **_cover.pdf**.

*(Internal ID: `c_coverSeparatePDF` · Config key: `cover/makeseparatePDF`)*

### Finishing tab

#### Booklet Pagination

- **Where:** Finishing tab
- **Type:** Label
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Whether you need a simple booklet or a more complex signature, these options allow plenty of scope.

#### Compare PDFs

- **Where:** Finishing tab
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Create 'diff' to Compare PDFs
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Enable this option to generate a PDF showing the differences between the current PDF and the selected previous version (see 'Compare With a Previous PDF' below).
>
> If any differences are found, it should open the "Diff" PDF in the default PDF viewer.
>
> Shortcut: Ctrl-R

**Explanation:**

When ticked, every **Print** also makes a "diff" PDF that shows the differences between the new PDF and the comparison PDF (see **Select...** in the **Compare PDFs** area). The diff PDF opens automatically. Untick it when you no longer need it, because comparing adds time to each print. When you untick it, PTXprint deletes the old diff file.

*(Internal ID: `c_createDiff`)*

### Finishing tab › Compare PDFs

#### Select...

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
- **Type:** Button
- **Description:** Compare PDFs: Select previous PDF to compare with
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Select a particular PDF file to be compared against the current output PDF. If you just want to compare output to the previous run, then click Cancel in the File Open dialog to reset the filename (which will then default to _1).

**Explanation:**

By default the comparison is with the previous run (**Previous PDF (_1)**). Use this button to choose a different PDF, such as the proof you sent for checking last month. The label becomes bold to remind you that a special file is selected. Click **Cancel** in the file dialog to go back to the previous run.

*(Internal ID: `btn_selectDiffPDF` · Config key: `document/diffpdf`)*

#### Only Show Pages With Differences

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
- **Type:** Checkbox (ticked by default)
- **Description:** Compare PDFs: Only show pages with differences
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> When comparing two PDF files the resulting "Diff" PDF can get rather large. This option reduces the size of the PDF by not including any identical pages. This also saves time as you don't need to search through a lengthy PDF to find out what might have changed.

**Explanation:**

Leave this ticked. Then the diff PDF contains only the pages that changed, so it is small and quick to check. Untick it only if you want to see every page, changed or not.

*(Internal ID: `c_onlyDiffs` · Config key: `document/onlyshowdiffs`)*

#### Show New Text or Position in

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
- **Type:** Colour picker
- **Description:** Compare PDFs:
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Use this color to show anything that has been added (or moved to the current location) in the new PDF.
>
> Set the color to use when differences are found between the old and the new PDFs.
>
> Use this color to show anything that has been added (or moved to the current location) in the new PDF.

**Explanation:**

The colour used in the diff PDF for new things: text that was added, or text that moved to this place. Choose a colour that is easy to tell apart from the **Show Old Text or Position in** colour.

*(Internal ID: `col_ndiffColor` · Config key: `document/ndiffcolor`)*

#### Show Old Text or Position in

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
- **Type:** Colour picker
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Use this color to show anything that has been deleted (or moved from the previous location) in the old PDF.
>
> Set the color to use when differences are found between the old and the new PDFs.
>
> Use this color to show anything that has been deleted (or moved from the previous location) in the old PDF.

**Explanation:**

The colour used in the diff PDF for old things: text that was removed, or the place where moved text used to be. Choose a colour that is easy to tell apart from the **Show New Text or Position in** colour.

*(Internal ID: `col_odiffColor` · Config key: `document/odiffcolor`)*

#### Show Max Diff Pages

- **Where:** Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
- **Type:** Number box
- **Description:** Compare PDFs: Set maximum diff pages to show
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Values:** from 1 to 999, default 20

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> The PDF showing differences between the old and the new contains images that make the resulting file rather large. Use this option to limit the number of "Diff" pages created. This will also potentially speed up the process.

**Explanation:**

The highest number of changed pages that are put into the diff PDF. Each diff page is an image, so many pages make a large file and take time. The default of 20 is usually enough. Increase it if you expect many pages to change, for example after a change that moves text across the whole book.

*(Internal ID: `s_diffpages` · Config key: `document/diffpages`)*

### Finishing tab › PDF Details

#### PDF Output Format

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Drop-down list
- **Description:** PDF output format (Screen, RGB, CMYK, B/W, spot)
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Choices:** Screen (Quickest); Digital-RGB; Digital-CMYK (Transparency); Print-CMYK; Print-Gray (B/W); Print-Spot

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Select the appropriate standard for the output format to optimize the PDF for its intended purpose.
>
> Screen (fastest, no post processing) Digital-RGB (for screens and local printing, PDF/X-4) Digital-CMYK (CMYK, PDF/X-4) Print-CMYK, Print-Gray (B/W), Print-Spot (for professional printers, PDF/X-1a:2003)
>
> Note: Tick 'Archive' to also comply with the archive standard PDF/A-4.

**Explanation:**

Use **Screen (Quickest)** while you work. Choose the final format only when you make the PDF for the printer: **Print-CMYK** for a printer that asks for PDF/X-1a or CMYK; **Print-Gray (B/W)** for black-ink-only books; **Print-Spot** for black plus one extra ink; **Digital-RGB** for screens, e-books and office printers (PDF/X-4). The non-Screen formats take longer to make, especially with many pictures. Each format adds its own ending to the file name (for example **_CMYK**), so the files do not overwrite each other.

*(Internal ID: `fcb_outputFormat` · Config key: `transparency_`, `snippets/pdfoutput`)*

#### PDF Output Format

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Label
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Select the appropriate standard for the output format to optimize the PDF for its intended purpose.
>
> Screen (fastest, no post processing) Digital-RGB (for screens and local printing, PDF/X-4) Digital-CMYK (CMYK, PDF/X-4) Print-CMYK, Print-Gray (B/W), Print-Spot (for professional printers, PDF/X-1a:2003)
>
> Note: Tick 'Archive' to also comply with the archive standard PDF/A-4.

#### Crop Marks

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Enable crop marks
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Some printers require crop marks on the PDF to show where the page should be trimmed after binding.

**Explanation:**

Adds cut marks at the corners of each page. PTXprint makes each PDF page 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) larger on every side to make room for them. Only tick this if your printer asks for crop marks; many print-on-demand printers reject files with crop marks because the page size is then wrong. When **Pages Per Spread** is 2-up or more, the marks are drawn on the large sheet instead.

*(Internal ID: `c_cropmarks` · Config key: `paper/cropmarks`)*

#### Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Number box
- **View level:** Default and Full views
- **Values:** default 1

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> By default, PTXprint only keeps one previous PDF (named ..._1.pdf). Up to 20 previous versions can be kept. Compare PDFs uses the _1 PDF unless you select another one, so keep at least 1.
>
> By keeping previous versions of the PDF, it is possible to compare the final output of the PDFs. Up to 20 previous versions can be kept.
>
> If you need to keep a PDF around longer, then manually rename it so that it can be compared to at a later date.

**Explanation:**

Before each new PDF is made, PTXprint copies the old one to a file ending **_1.pdf** (and the older ones to **_2.pdf**, **_3.pdf** …). **Compare PDFs** uses the **_1** file, so keep this at 1 or more if you want to compare. Older versions are deleted when the number is reached, so rename a PDF yourself if you must keep it.

*(Internal ID: `s_keepVersions` · Config key: `document/keepversions`)*

#### Include Config Settings Within PDF

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Checkbox (ticked by default)
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> All the configuration settings (including the PTXprint styles, AdjLists, changes.txt, and related .tex files) can be included within the PDF in order to maintain a record of what settings were used to create that PDF. Later, these settings can be retrieved from the PDF to set up an identical configuration. This is also a way to share config settings with other users.

**Explanation:**

Stores your configuration (settings, styles, AdjLists, changes and related files) inside the PDF file. The PDF looks the same. It is a good record of how the PDF was made. You or another person can load these settings back with **Import Settings**, choosing the PDF as the source. Leave it ticked unless you have a reason not to share your settings with the PDF.

*(Internal ID: `c_inclSettingsInPDF` · Config key: `document/settingsinpdf`, `finishing/inclsettings`)*

#### Archive (PDF/A-4)

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Include unicode text within PDF (to help with archiving)
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Check this option to include the Unicode text in the PDF which is a good practice for final print and long-term archiving. PDF/A-4 is the currently preferred archival format.

**Explanation:**

Makes a PDF that follows the PDF/A-4 archive standard. The text in the PDF can then be searched and copied correctly as Unicode, which is good for long-term storage and for digital libraries. Only tick it if you need an archive PDF; it is not needed for normal printing.

*(Internal ID: `c_printArchive` · Config key: `document/printarchive`)*

#### Color Hue

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Colour picker
- **Description:** Spot color hue
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> If a spot color is needed then select the closest hue. Colors close to this hue are printed with the spot ink; everything else in black/gray. Tell your printer which ink to use.

**Explanation:**

Only active when **PDF Output Format** is **Print-Spot**. Choose the colour (hue) of the spot ink, for example the red used for headings. Text and graphics with a similar colour are printed with the spot ink; everything else becomes black and grey. Tell your printer which ink (for example, which Pantone number) they should use for this colour.

*(Internal ID: `col_spotColor` · Config key: `finishing/spotcolor`)*

#### Tolerance (%)

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Number box
- **Description:** Spot color tolerance
- **View level:** Full view only
- **Values:** default 15

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> To match the Spot Color Hue exactly, set this to 0%. If text in similar colors are also to be set to this Spot Color, then select an acceptable tolerance range (suggested default is 15%).
>
> Note that this will include similar colors either side (e.g. -15% to +15%) of the selected hue.

**Explanation:**

Only active when **PDF Output Format** is **Print-Spot**. Sets how close a colour must be to the **Color Hue** to be printed with the spot ink. 0% means only exactly that hue. The default of 15% also catches slightly different shades. Increase it if some coloured items come out grey; decrease it if items that should be grey come out in the spot colour.

*(Internal ID: `s_spotColorTolerance` · Config key: `finishing/spottolerance`, `color/spotcolrange`)*

#### Extract Color Inserts

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Extract Color Insert pages (as separate PDFs)
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Extract the special peripheral materials named 'maps' or 'insert_*' as separate PDFs to be printed in color and inserted manually during the binding process.
>
> Note that the cover is always extracted.

**Explanation:**

Takes special pages out of the main PDF and saves them as separate PDF files: maps, and peripheral pages whose name starts with "insert_". The new file names end with the name of the insert, for example **_maps.pdf**. Use this when colour pages are printed separately and added to the book during binding. The extracted pages are removed from the main PDF.

*(Internal ID: `c_extractInserts` · Config key: `finishing/extractinserts`)*

#### Extra XDV Processing

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Extra XDV processing (before creating final PDF)
- **View level:** Full view only

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

> Enable processing of the intermediate xdv file for such things as coloured diacritics.

**Explanation:**

Runs an extra processing step before the final PDF is made. It is needed only for a few special features, such as coloured diacritics. Leave it unticked unless a feature you use asks for it, because it makes printing slower.

*(Internal ID: `c_extraxdvproc` · Config key: `finishing/extraxdvproc`)*

#### Apply Watermark PDF

- **Where:** Finishing tab › PDF Details
- **Type:** Checkbox (not ticked by default)
- **Description:** Finishing: Apply watermark
- **View level:** Default and Full views

**Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):**

**Explanation:**

Adds a watermark PDF behind every page, for example the word "DRAFT" or a copyright notice. This is helpful for proof copies, so that nobody mistakes them for the finished book. Untick it before you make the final PDF for the printer. The watermark PDF should have the same page size as your book.
